It is recited with the *idafah* (the genitive construction, "adornment of the stars") and with the *badal* (apposition, "adornment, the stars"), and both have the same meaning. His saying here, ﴿and as a protection﴾, its estimate is: "and We protected it with protection." ﴿From every rebellious devil﴾ means the defiant, insolent one, who, when he wants to steal a hearing, a piercing flaming fire comes to him and burns him. For this reason He said: ﴿They cannot listen to the exalted assembly﴾, meaning, so that they cannot reach the exalted assembly, which is the heavens and those in them of the angels, when they speak of what Allah reveals of His legislation and His decree, as the explanation of this has already passed in the narrations we cited at His saying, exalted is He: ﴿until, when fear is removed from their hearts, they say, "What has your Lord said?" They say, "The truth, and He is the Exalted, the Great"﴾ [Saba': 23]. For this reason He said ﴿and they are pelted﴾, meaning they are struck, ﴿from every side﴾, meaning from every direction from which they aim at the heaven, ﴿repulsed﴾, meaning stoned, by which they are driven off and repelled and prevented from reaching that. ﴿And for them is a perpetual punishment﴾, meaning in the Hereafter they have a lasting, painful, continuous punishment, as He said: ﴿And We have prepared for them the punishment of the Blaze﴾ [al-Mulk: 5].

Perhaps the meteor overtakes him before he throws it, and perhaps he throws it by the decree of Allah before the meteor reaches him and burns him. Then the other carries it off to the soothsayer, as has passed in the hadith. For this reason He said: ﴿except one who snatches a snatch, so he is pursued by a piercing flame﴾, meaning a shining one.

He said: So they complained of that to Iblis, and he said: "This is nothing but a matter that has occurred." He said: So he dispatched his armies, and behold, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was standing praying between the two mountains of Nakhlah. He said: Waki' said: meaning the valley of Nakhlah. He said: So they returned to Iblis and informed him, and he said: "This is the thing that has occurred."

He said: ﴿And there is none of you but will arrive at it [Hell]. That has been against your Lord a decree [that must be] carried out. Therefore He said here: ﴿except the sincere servants of Allah﴾, meaning: they will not taste the painful punishment, nor will they be scrutinized in the reckoning. Rather, He will overlook their misdeeds, if they have any, and their good deeds will be multiplied tenfold up to seven hundred times, and to many more multiples, as much as Allah wills by way of multiplication.

* *

His saying: ﴿For them is a known provision﴾. Qatadah and As-Suddi said: it means Paradise. Then He explained it with His saying: ﴿fruits﴾, meaning varied, ﴿and they will be honored﴾, meaning they will be served [and provided for], and made comfortable and given luxury, ﴿in gardens of pleasure, upon thrones facing one another﴾. Mujahid said: none of them looks at the back of another.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Yahya ibn Abdak al-Qazwini narrated to us; Hassan ibn Hassan narrated to us; Ibrahim ibn Bishr narrated to us; Yahya ibn Ma'in narrated to us; Ibrahim al-Qurashi narrated to us, from Sa'id ibn Shurahbil, from Zayd ibn Abi Awfa, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came out to us and recited this verse: ﴿upon thrones facing one another﴾, [meaning] they look at one another.

This is a strange (gharib) hadith. [Al-Bukhari mentioned it in at-Tarikh al-Kabir (3/386) in the biography of Zayd ibn Abi Awfa, through the chain of Hassan ibn Hassan, and said: "No one else narrates it."]

* *

His saying: ﴿They will be served with a cup from a flowing spring, white, delicious to the drinkers, neither will there be in it intoxication, nor will they be depleted by it﴾. As He said in another verse: ﴿There will circulate among them young boys made eternal, with cups and jugs and a cup from a flowing spring; they will not be affected by headache from it, nor will they be intoxicated﴾ [Al-Waqi'ah: 17-19]. So Allah has purified the wine of the Hereafter [in Paradise] from the afflictions found in the wine of this world: from headache, stomach pain (which is al-ghawl), and its complete removal of the intellect. Here He said: ﴿They will be served with a cup from a flowing spring﴾, meaning: with wine from flowing rivers, which they do not fear will cease or run out.

Malik narrated from Zayd ibn Aslam: "Wine that flows, white," meaning its color is bright, fine, and pleasing, unlike the wine of this world with its repulsive and inferior appearance, of redness, blackness, yellowness, or turbidity, and other things that repel a sound nature.

* *

Ibn Kathir's commentary on Surah 37, verses 50–61 (part 1 of 2):

Allah the Exalted informs about the people of Paradise that some of them will turn toward others, asking one another (yatasa'alun), that is, about their conditions and how they were in the world, and what they used to suffer in it. This will be part of their conversation over their drinks, their gathering in their companionship and fellowship in their assemblies, while they sit on couches (al-sururs), with servants before them, running about and bringing every great good: foods, drinks, garments, and other things that no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and that have never occurred to the heart of any human being.[[In A: "sarratahum" (their best).]]

﴿One of them will say, "I had a companion."﴾ Mujahid said: he means a devil (shaytan).

Al-Awfi related from Ibn Abbas: he is the polytheist man who had a companion among the people of faith in the world.

There is no contradiction between the statement of Mujahid and that of Ibn Abbas, for the devil may be from the jinn, who whispers into the soul, or from mankind, who speaks words that the two ears hear. Both are enemies of the believer. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿They inspire one another with ornamented speech as deception﴾ [al-An'am 6:112]. Each of them whispers, as the Exalted said: ﴿Say: I seek refuge in the Lord of mankind, the King of mankind, the God of mankind, from the evil of the sneaking whisperer, who whispers in the breasts of mankind, of the jinn and of mankind﴾ [an-Nas 114:1–6].[[Added from T, S, A.]] Therefore, ﴿one of them will say, "I had a companion who would say, 'Are you really among those who believe?'"﴾ That is: do you truly believe in the Resurrection, the gathering, the reckoning and the recompense? He says this out of astonishment, denial, disbelief, and obstinacy. ﴿"When we have died and become dust and bones, shall we indeed be held to account?"﴾ Mujahid and al-Suddi said: "Shall we be called to account?" Ibn Abbas and Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi said: "Shall we be recompensed for our deeds?"

Allah said: ﴿He will say, "Will you look down?"﴾ That is, will you look over (mushrifun). The believer says this to his companions and associates among the people of Paradise. ﴿Then he looked down and saw him in the midst of the Blazing Fire.﴾ Ibn Abbas, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Khulayd al-Asri, Qatadah, al-Suddi, Ata al-Khurasani, and others said: in the midst of the Hellfire.

Al-Hasan al-Basri said: in the midst of the Hellfire, like a blazing meteor.

Qatadah said: It was related to us that he looked down and saw the skulls of the people boiling. It was also related to us that Ka'b al-Ahbar said: "In Paradise there are openings, so that when one of its people wishes to look at his enemy in the Fire, he looks through them, and his gratitude increases."

﴿He will say, "By Allah, you almost brought me to ruin.﴾ The believer says this to the disbeliever: "By Allah, you nearly destroyed me had I obeyed you. ﴿Had it not been for the grace of my Lord, I would have been among those brought forth [to the punishment].﴾" That is: had it not been for the favor of Allah upon me, I would have been like you in the midst of the Hellfire, where you are, brought forth with you in the punishment. But He showed me favor and mercy, guided me to faith, and directed me to His oneness. ﴿And we would not have been guided had Allah not guided us﴾ [al-A'raf 7:43].

* *

His saying: ﴿Shall we not die, except for our first death, and shall we not be punished?﴾ This is from the speech of the believer, who is delighting in what Allah has given him of eternity in Paradise and of dwelling in the abode of honor, where there is no death and no punishment. Therefore He said: ﴿Indeed, this is the great triumph.﴾

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Abd Allah al-Zahrani related to us, Hafs ibn Umar al-Adani related to us, al-Hakam ibn Aban related to us, from Ikrimah, who said: Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, said concerning the saying of Allah the Blessed and Exalted to the people of Paradise: ﴿Eat and drink with pleasure for what you used to do﴾ [at-Tur 52:19]: Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: His saying "with pleasure" (hanian) means that they do not die therein. Thereupon they said: ﴿Shall we not die, except for our first death, and shall we not be punished?﴾

Al-Hasan al-Basri said: They knew that every blessing is cut off by death, so they said: ﴿Shall we not die, except for our first death, and shall we not be punished?﴾ It was said to them: "No." They said: ﴿Indeed, this is the great triumph.﴾

* *

His saying: ﴿For the like of this let the workers work﴾. Qatadah said: this is from the speech of the people of Paradise.

Ibn Jarir said: it is from the speech of Allah the Exalted, and its meaning is: for the like of this blessing and this triumph, let the workers work in the world, so that they may arrive at it in the Hereafter.[[Tafsir al-Tabari (23/40).]]

They have also mentioned the story of two men who were partners among the Children of Israel, which falls within the general scope of this noble verse.

Abu Ja'far ibn Jarir said: Ishaq ibn Ibrahim ibn Habib ibn al-Shahid related to me, Attab ibn Bashir related to us, from Khusayf, from Furat ibn Thalabah al-Bahrani, concerning His saying: ﴿I had a companion﴾: He said: Two men were partners, and they accumulated eight thousand dinars. One of them had a trade, and the other had no trade. The one with a trade said to the other: "You have no trade. I see nothing for me but to separate from you and divide the property." So he divided it with him and parted from him. Then the man bought a house for a thousand dinars that had belonged to a king who had died. He called his companion, showed it to him, and said: "How do you find this house? I bought it for a thousand dinars." He said: "How beautiful it is!" When he left, [the first] said: "O Allah, my companion has bought this house for a thousand dinars, and I ask You for a house from the houses of Paradise." So he gave a thousand dinars in charity. Allah the Exalted informs about the people of Paradise that some of them will turn toward others, asking one another (yatasa'alun), that is, about their conditions and how they were in the world, and what they used to suffer in it. This will be part of their conversation over their drinks, their gathering in their companionship and fellowship in their assemblies, while they sit on couches (al-sururs), with servants before them, running about and bringing every great good: foods, drinks, garments, and other things that no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and that have never occurred to the heart of any human being.[[In A: "sarratahum" (their best).]]

﴿One of them will say, "I had a companion."﴾ Mujahid said: he means a devil (shaytan).

Al-Awfi related from Ibn Abbas: he is the polytheist man who had a companion among the people of faith in the world.

There is no contradiction between the statement of Mujahid and that of Ibn Abbas, for the devil may be from the jinn, who whispers into the soul, or from mankind, who speaks words that the two ears hear. Both are enemies of the believer. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿They inspire one another with ornamented speech as deception﴾ [al-An'am 6:112]. Each of them whispers, as the Exalted said: ﴿Say: I seek refuge in the Lord of mankind, the King of mankind, the God of mankind, from the evil of the sneaking whisperer, who whispers in the breasts of mankind, of the jinn and of mankind﴾ [an-Nas 114:1–6].[[Added from T, S, A.]] Therefore, ﴿one of them will say, "I had a companion who would say, 'Are you really among those who believe?'"﴾ That is: do you truly believe in the Resurrection, the gathering, the reckoning and the recompense? He says this out of astonishment, denial, disbelief, and obstinacy. ﴿"When we have died and become dust and bones, shall we indeed be held to account?"﴾ Mujahid and al-Suddi said: "Shall we be called to account?" Ibn Abbas and Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi said: "Shall we be recompensed for our deeds?"

Qatadah said: It was related to us that he looked down and saw the skulls of the people boiling. Ibn Kathir's commentary on Surah 37, verses 50–61 (part 1 of 2):

Allah the Exalted informs about the people of Paradise that some of them will turn toward others, asking one another (yatasa'alun), that is, about their conditions and how they were in the world, and what they used to suffer in it. This will be part of their conversation over their drinks, their gathering in their companionship and fellowship in their assemblies, while they sit on couches (al-sururs), with servants before them, running about and bringing every great good: foods, drinks, garments, and other things that no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and that have never occurred to the heart of any human being.[[In A: "sarratahum" (their best).]]

﴿One of them will say, "I had a companion."﴾ Mujahid said: he means a devil (shaytan).

Al-Awfi related from Ibn Abbas: he is the polytheist man who had a companion among the people of faith in the world.

There is no contradiction between the statement of Mujahid and that of Ibn Abbas, for the devil may be from the jinn, who whispers into the soul, or from mankind, who speaks words that the two ears hear. Both are enemies of the believer. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿They inspire one another with ornamented speech as deception﴾ [al-An'am 6:112]. Each of them whispers, as the Exalted said: ﴿Say: I seek refuge in the Lord of mankind, the King of mankind, the God of mankind, from the evil of the sneaking whisperer, who whispers in the breasts of mankind, of the jinn and of mankind﴾ [an-Nas 114:1–6].[[Added from T, S, A.]] Therefore, ﴿one of them will say, "I had a companion who would say, 'Are you really among those who believe?'"﴾ That is: do you truly believe in the Resurrection, the gathering, the reckoning and the recompense? He says this out of astonishment, denial, disbelief, and obstinacy. ﴿"When we have died and become dust and bones, shall we indeed be held to account?"﴾ Mujahid and al-Suddi said: "Shall we be called to account?" Ibn Abbas and Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi said: "Shall we be recompensed for our deeds?"

Allah said: ﴿He will say, "Will you look down?"﴾ That is, will you look over (mushrifun). The believer says this to his companions and associates among the people of Paradise. ﴿Then he looked down and saw him in the midst of the Blazing Fire.﴾ Ibn Abbas, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Khulayd al-Asri, Qatadah, al-Suddi, Ata al-Khurasani, and others said: in the midst of the Hellfire.

﴿One of them will say, "I had a companion."﴾ Mujahid said: he means a devil (shaytan).

Al-Awfi related from Ibn Abbas: he is the polytheist man who had a companion among the people of faith in the world.

Ibn Abbas and Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi said: "Shall we be recompensed for our deeds?"

Ibn Kathir's commentary on Surah 37, verses 50–61 (part 1 of 2):

Allah the Exalted informs about the people of Paradise that some of them will turn toward others, asking one another (yatasa'alun), that is, about their conditions and how they were in the world, and what they used to suffer in it. This will be part of their conversation over their drinks, their gathering in their companionship and fellowship in their assemblies, while they sit on couches (al-sururs), with servants before them, running about and bringing every great good: foods, drinks, garments, and other things that no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and that have never occurred to the heart of any human being.[[In A: "sarratahum" (their best).]]

﴿One of them will say, "I had a companion."﴾ Mujahid said: he means a devil (shaytan).

Al-Awfi related from Ibn Abbas: he is the polytheist man who had a companion among the people of faith in the world.

There is no contradiction between the statement of Mujahid and that of Ibn Abbas, for the devil may be from the jinn, who whispers into the soul, or from mankind, who speaks words that the two ears hear. Both are enemies of the believer. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿They inspire one another with ornamented speech as deception﴾ [al-An'am 6:112]. Each of them whispers, as the Exalted said: ﴿Say: I seek refuge in the Lord of mankind, the King of mankind, the God of mankind, from the evil of the sneaking whisperer, who whispers in the breasts of mankind, of the jinn and of mankind﴾ [an-Nas 114:1–6].[[Added from T, S, A.]] Therefore, ﴿one of them will say, "I had a companion who would say, 'Are you really among those who believe?'"﴾ That is: do you truly believe in the Resurrection, the gathering, the reckoning and the recompense? He says this out of astonishment, denial, disbelief, and obstinacy. ﴿"When we have died and become dust and bones, shall we indeed be held to account?"﴾ Mujahid and al-Suddi said: "Shall we be called to account?" Ibn Abbas and Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi said: "Shall we be recompensed for our deeds?"

Allah said: ﴿He will say, "Will you look down?"﴾ That is, will you look over (mushrifun). The believer says this to his companions and associates among the people of Paradise. ﴿Then he looked down and saw him in the midst of the Blazing Fire.﴾ Ibn Abbas, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Khulayd al-Asri, Qatadah, al-Suddi, Ata al-Khurasani, and others said: in the midst of the Hellfire.

Al-Hasan al-Basri said: in the midst of the Hellfire, like a blazing meteor.

Qatadah said: It was related to us that he looked down and saw the skulls of the people boiling. It was also related to us that Ka'b al-Ahbar said: "In Paradise there are openings, so that when one of its people wishes to look at his enemy in the Fire, he looks through them, and his gratitude increases."

﴿He will say, "By Allah, you almost brought me to ruin.﴾ The believer says this to the disbeliever: "By Allah, you nearly destroyed me had I obeyed you. ﴿Had it not been for the grace of my Lord, I would have been among those brought forth [to the punishment].﴾" That is: had it not been for the favor of Allah upon me, I would have been like you in the midst of the Hellfire, where you are, brought forth with you in the punishment. Allah the Exalted informs about the people of Paradise that some of them will turn toward others, asking one another (yatasa'alun), that is, about their conditions and how they were in the world, and what they used to suffer in it. This will be part of their conversation over their drinks, their gathering in their companionship and fellowship in their assemblies, while they sit on couches (al-sururs), with servants before them, running about and bringing every great good: foods, drinks, garments, and other things that no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and that have never occurred to the heart of any human being.[[In A: "sarratahum" (their best).]]

﴿One of them will say, "I had a companion."﴾ Mujahid said: he means a devil (shaytan).

Al-Awfi related from Ibn Abbas: he is the polytheist man who had a companion among the people of faith in the world.

There is no contradiction between the statement of Mujahid and that of Ibn Abbas, for the devil may be from the jinn, who whispers into the soul, or from mankind, who speaks words that the two ears hear. Both are enemies of the believer. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿They inspire one another with ornamented speech as deception﴾ [al-An'am 6:112]. Each of them whispers, as the Exalted said: ﴿Say: I seek refuge in the Lord of mankind, the King of mankind, the God of mankind, from the evil of the sneaking whisperer, who whispers in the breasts of mankind, of the jinn and of mankind﴾ [an-Nas 114:1–6].[[Added from T, S, A.]] Therefore, ﴿one of them will say, "I had a companion who would say, 'Are you really among those who believe?'"﴾ That is: do you truly believe in the Resurrection, the gathering, the reckoning and the recompense? He says this out of astonishment, denial, disbelief, and obstinacy. ﴿"When we have died and become dust and bones, shall we indeed be held to account?"﴾ Mujahid and al-Suddi said: "Shall we be called to account?" Ibn Abbas and Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi said: "Shall we be recompensed for our deeds?"

Allah said: ﴿He will say, "Will you look down?"﴾ That is, will you look over (mushrifun). The believer says this to his companions and associates among the people of Paradise. ﴿Then he looked down and saw him in the midst of the Blazing Fire.﴾ Ibn Abbas, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Khulayd al-Asri, Qatadah, al-Suddi, Ata al-Khurasani, and others said: in the midst of the Hellfire.

Al-Hasan al-Basri said: in the midst of the Hellfire, like a blazing meteor.

Qatadah said: It was related to us that he looked down and saw the skulls of the people boiling. It was also related to us that Ka'b al-Ahbar said: "In Paradise there are openings, so that when one of its people wishes to look at his enemy in the Fire, he looks through them, and his gratitude increases."

﴿He will say, "By Allah, you almost brought me to ruin.﴾ The believer says this to the disbeliever: "By Allah, you nearly destroyed me had I obeyed you. ﴿Had it not been for the grace of my Lord, I would have been among those brought forth [to the punishment].﴾" That is: had it not been for the favor of Allah upon me, I would have been like you in the midst of the Hellfire, where you are, brought forth with you in the punishment. But He showed me favor and mercy, guided me to faith, and directed me to His oneness. ﴿And we would not have been guided had Allah not guided us﴾ [al-A'raf 7:43].

* *

His saying: ﴿Shall we not die, except for our first death, and shall we not be punished?﴾ This is from the speech of the believer, who is delighting in what Allah has given him of eternity in Paradise and of dwelling in the abode of honor, where there is no death and no punishment. Therefore He said: ﴿Indeed, this is the great triumph.﴾

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Abd Allah al-Zahrani related to us, Hafs ibn Umar al-Adani related to us, al-Hakam ibn Aban related to us, from Ikrimah, who said: Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, said concerning the saying of Allah the Blessed and Exalted to the people of Paradise: ﴿Eat and drink with pleasure for what you used to do﴾ [at-Tur 52:19]: Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: His saying "with pleasure" (hanian) means that they do not die therein. Thereupon they said: ﴿Shall we not die, except for our first death, and shall we not be punished?﴾

Al-Hasan al-Basri said: They knew that every blessing is cut off by death, so they said: ﴿Shall we not die, except for our first death, and shall we not be punished?﴾ It was said to them: "No." They said: ﴿Indeed, this is the great triumph.﴾

* *

His saying: ﴿For the like of this let the workers work﴾. Qatadah said: this is from the speech of the people of Paradise.

Ibn Jarir said: it is from the speech of Allah the Exalted, and its meaning is: for the like of this blessing and this triumph, let the workers work in the world, so that they may arrive at it in the Hereafter.[[Tafsir al-Tabari (23/40).]]

They have also mentioned the story of two men who were partners among the Children of Israel, which falls within the general scope of this noble verse.

Abu Ja'far ibn Jarir said: Ishaq ibn Ibrahim ibn Habib ibn al-Shahid related to me, Attab ibn Bashir related to us, from Khusayf, from Furat ibn Thalabah al-Bahrani, concerning His saying: ﴿I had a companion﴾: He said: Two men were partners, and they accumulated eight thousand dinars. One of them had a trade, and the other had no trade. The one with a trade said to the other: "You have no trade. I see nothing for me but to separate from you and divide the property." So he divided it with him and parted from him. Then the man bought a house for a thousand dinars that had belonged to a king who had died. He called his companion, showed it to him, and said: "How do you find this house? I bought it for a thousand dinars." He said: "How beautiful it is!" When he left, [the first] said: "O Allah, my companion has bought this house for a thousand dinars, and I ask You for a house from the houses of Paradise." So he gave a thousand dinars in charity. Then he remained as long as Allah willed him to remain. Then he married a woman for a thousand dinars, and he invited his companion and prepared food for him. When he came, he said: "I have married a woman for a thousand dinars." He said: "How good this is!" When he left, [the first] said: "O Lord, my companion has married a woman for a thousand dinars, and I ask You for a woman of the wide-eyed maidens (al-hur al-in)." So he gave a thousand dinars in charity. Then he remained as long as Allah willed him to remain. Then he bought two gardens for two thousand dinars. Then he called his companion, showed them to him, and said: "I have bought these two gardens." He said: "How beautiful this is!" When he left, [the first] said: "O Lord, my companion has bought two gardens for two thousand dinars, and I ask You for two gardens in Paradise." So he gave two thousand dinars in charity. Then the Angel came to them both and took their souls. Then he took this one who gave charity away, and brought him into a house that delighted him, and there was a woman appearing, whose beauty lit up what was beneath her. Then he brought him into two gardens containing things that only Allah knows. He said at that point: "How similar this is to a man whose affair was such and such." It was said: "That is indeed what it is, and for you is this abode, the two gardens, and the woman." He said: "My companion used to say: 'Are you really among those who believe?'" It was said to him: "Indeed he is in the Hellfire." He said: "Will you look down?" He looked down and saw him in the midst of the Blazing Fire. Thereupon he said: ﴿By Allah, you almost brought me to ruin. Had it not been for the grace of my Lord, I would have been among those brought forth﴾, and the verses that follow.

Ibn Jarir said: This strengthens the recitation of those who read: "Innaka la-mina al-mussaddiqin" (أَئِنَّكَ لَمِنَ المُصَّدّقِينَ) with the doubled letter (tashdid).

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Al-Hasan ibn 'Arafah narrated to us, saying: 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Abbar Abu Hafs narrated to us, saying: I asked Isma'il al-Suddi about this verse: ﴿A speaker among them will say, "Indeed, I had a companion who used to say, 'Are you really among those who believe?'"﴾ He said to me: "What prompted you to this?" I said: "I recited it just now, and I wanted to ask you about it." He said: "Listen. There were two partners among the Children of Israel, one of them a believer and the other a disbeliever. They parted ways with six thousand dinars, each of them taking three thousand dinars. They remained together for as long as Allah willed them to remain. Then they met, and the disbeliever said to the believer: 'What have you done with your wealth? Have you invested it in anything? Have you traded with it in anything?' The believer said to him: 'No. What have you done?' He said: 'I bought with it land, palm trees, fruits and rivers [in another version: and rivers for a thousand dinars].' The believer said to him: 'Really? Have you done that?' He said: 'Yes.' The believer returned, and when night came he prayed as much as Allah willed him to pray. When he finished, he took a thousand dinars and placed them before him, then said: 'O Allah, indeed so-and-so, meaning his disbelieving partner, has bought land, palm trees, fruits and rivers for a thousand dinars, and he will die tomorrow and leave them behind. O Allah, I have bought from You, with these thousand dinars, land, palm trees, fruits and rivers in Paradise.' He said: Then he rose in the morning and distributed them among the poor. He said: Then they remained together for as long as Allah willed them to remain, and then they met, and the disbeliever said to the believer: 'What have you done with your wealth? Have you invested it in anything? Have you traded with it in anything?' He said: 'No. What have you done?' He said: 'My estate had become a heavy burden on me in its upkeep, so I bought with a thousand dinars slaves who would tend to me in it and work for me in it.' The believer said to him: 'Really? Have you done that?' He said: 'Yes.' He said: The believer returned, and when night came he prayed as much as Allah willed him to pray. When he finished, he took a thousand dinars and placed them before him, and said: 'O Allah, indeed so-and-so, meaning his disbelieving partner, has bought slaves from the slaves of this world with a thousand dinars; he will die tomorrow and leave them, or they will die and leave him. O Allah, I am buying from You, with these thousand dinars, slaves in Paradise.' Then he rose in the morning and distributed them among the poor. He said: Then they remained together for as long as Allah the Exalted willed them to remain, then they met, and the disbeliever said to the believer: 'What have you done with your wealth? Have you invested it in anything? Have you traded with it in anything?' He said: 'No. What have you done?' He said: 'My whole affair has been completed, except for one thing: a woman whose husband has died, and I gave her a dowry of a thousand dinars; she came to me with them and the like of them with her.' The believer said to him: 'Really? Have you done that?' He said: 'Yes.' The believer returned, and when night came he prayed as much as Allah willed him to pray. When he finished, he took the remaining thousand dinars and placed them before him, and said: 'O Allah, indeed so-and-so, meaning his disbelieving partner, has married a wife from the wives of this world, and he will die tomorrow and leave her, or he will die and she will leave him. O Allah, and I propose to You, with these thousand dinars, a wide-eyed houri in Paradise.' Then he rose in the morning and distributed them among the poor. He said: The believer was left with nothing. He said: He put on a shirt of cotton and a cloak of wool, then took a pickaxe and placed it on his neck, doing work and digging with his strength. He said: A man came to him and said: 'O servant of Allah, will you hire yourself out to me monthly, month by month, to attend to my animals, feeding them and sweeping their dung?' He said: 'Yes.' He said: So he hired himself out to him monthly, month by month, to attend to his animals. He said: The owner of the animals would go out every day to look at his animals, and if he saw one of them emaciated, he would take hold of its head and strike its neck, then say to it: 'Did you steal the barley of this one last night?' When the believer saw this severity, he said: 'I will go to my disbelieving partner, and I will work on his land, and he will feed me this morsel day by day and clothe me with these two garments when they wear out.' He said: He set out intending him, and when he reached his door in the evening, there was a lofty palace raised in the sky, and around it were gatekeepers. He said to them: 'Ask permission for me from the owner of this palace, for if you do so, it will please him.' They said to him: 'Go, if you are truthful; sleep in a corner, and when you rise in the morning, present yourself to him.' He said: The believer went, and he spread half his cloak beneath him and half above him, and slept. When he rose in the morning, he came to his partner and presented himself to him. His disbelieving partner came out riding, and when he saw him he recognized him, so he stopped over him, greeted him, and shook his hand, then said to him: 'Did you not take from the wealth the like of what I took?' He said: 'Yes, and this is my condition, and this is your condition.' He said: 'Tell me, what have you done with your wealth?' He said: 'Do not ask me about it.' He said: 'Then what brought you?' He said: 'I came to work on this land of yours, that you would feed me this morsel day by day and clothe me with these two garments when they wear out.' He said: 'No, but I will do for you what is better than this; but you will not see any good from me until you tell me what you did with your wealth.' He said: 'I lent it.' He said: 'To whom?' He said: 'To the Generous, the Faithful.' He said: 'To whom?' He said: 'To Allah, my Lord.' He said: While he was shaking his hand, he snatched his hand from his, then said: ﴿Are you really among those who believe? Is it that when we die and become dust and bones, we shall indeed be held to account?﴾ — al-Suddi said: "Called to account." He said: So the disbeliever went away and left him. He said: When the believer saw that he did not turn to him, he returned and left him. The believer lived in hardship of time, and the disbeliever lived in ease of time. He said: On the Day of Resurrection, when Allah admits the believer into Paradise, he will pass by, and behold, there is land, palm trees, fruits and rivers, and he will say: 'To whom does this belong?' It will be said: 'This is yours.' He will say: 'Glory be to Allah! Has my good deed reached such a degree that I should be rewarded with the like of this?!' He said: Then he will pass by, and behold, there are slaves whose number cannot be counted, and he will say: 'To whom do these belong?' It will be said: 'These are for you.' He will say: 'Glory be to Allah! Has my good deed reached such a degree that I should be rewarded with the like of this?!' He said: Then he will pass by, and behold, there is a dome of red ruby, hollowed out, in which is a wide-eyed houri, and he will say: 'To whom does this belong?' It will be said: 'This is yours.' He will say: 'Glory be to Allah! Has my good deed reached such a degree that I should be rewarded with the like of this?!' He said: Then the believer will remember his disbelieving partner and say: ﴿Indeed, I had a companion who used to say, "Are you really among those who believe? Is it that when we die and become dust and bones, we shall indeed be held to account?"﴾ He said: Then Paradise is on high, and Hellfire is an abyss. He said: Allah will show him his partner in the midst of Hellfire, among the people of the Fire. When the believer sees him, he recognizes him, and says: ﴿By Allah, you nearly ruined me! Had it not been for the favor of my Lord, I would have been among those brought forth. Is it not that we shall not die, except our first death, and we shall not be punished? Indeed, this is the great triumph. For the like of this let the workers work.﴾ — in the same manner as what was bestowed upon him. He said: Then the believer will remember the hardship he endured in the world, and nothing that he endured of hardship in the world will seem more severe to him than death. [This is one of the narratives from the Children of Israel on which no reliance is placed.]

Almighty Allah says: Is this (what He has mentioned of the bounties of Paradise and what is in it of foods, drinks, spouses and other pleasures) better as hospitality and gift, ﴿or the tree of zaqqum?﴾ That is, the one that is in Jahannam (Hellfire).

It may be that what is meant is one specific tree. Some have said it is a tree whose branches extend to every dwelling of Hellfire, just as the tree of Tuba is such that there is no house in Paradise except that it has a branch of it in it.

It may also be that what is meant is a kind of tree called zaqqum, as in His saying: ﴿And a tree that springs forth from Mount Sinai, which produces oil and a condiment for those who eat﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 20], meaning the olive tree. What supports this is His saying: ﴿Then indeed you, O astray deniers, will be eaters from a tree of zaqqum﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 51-52].

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Indeed, We have made it a trial for the wrongdoers﴾, Qatadah said: When the tree of zaqqum was mentioned, the people of misguidance were tested by it, and they said: "Your companion tells you that there is a tree in the Fire, while the Fire consumes trees!" So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿Indeed, it is a tree that springs up from the root of Hellfire﴾, nourished by the Fire, and created from it.

Mujahid said: ﴿Indeed, We have made it a trial for the wrongdoers﴾: Abu Jahl, may Allah curse him, said: "Zaqqum is only dates and butter; I will eat it (zaqqum)."

I say: The meaning of the verse is: "We only informed you, O Muhammad, about the tree of zaqqum as a test by which you examine the people, to know who among them believes and who denies," as in His saying: ﴿And We did not make the vision which We showed you except as a trial for the people, and [like] the accursed tree in the Qur'an. And We threaten them, but it increases them not except in great transgression﴾ [al-Isra': 60].

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Indeed, it is a tree that springs up from the root of Hellfire﴾, that is, the root of its growth is in the depths of the Fire. ﴿Its emerging fruit is like the heads of devils﴾, which is a way of describing it as hideous and making its mention repugnant.

Wahb ibn Munabbih said: "The hair of the devils is raised toward the sky."

It was likened to the heads of devils even though they were not known to the addressees, because it is firmly established in souls that devils are ugly in appearance.

It was also said: what is meant is a kind of venomous snake, whose heads are hideous in appearance.

And it was said: it is a kind of plant whose flower is extremely foul.

There is scrutiny regarding these last two interpretations; Ibn Jarir mentioned them, and the first is stronger and more preferable. And Allah knows best.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Then indeed, they will be eaters from it and filling their bellies from it﴾, Allah mentions that they will eat from this tree, which has no more repulsive or hideous appearance, along with its bad taste, smell and nature. They will be compelled to eat from it because they will find nothing but it or what is similar to it, as He said: ﴿No food will there be for them except from fountain thorn. Which neither nourishes nor satisfies from hunger﴾ [al-Ghashiyah: 6-7].

Ibn Abi Hatim, may Allah have mercy on him, said: My father related to us, ʿAmr ibn Marzuq related to us, Shu'bah related to us, from al-A'mash, from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited this verse and said: "Fear Allah with the fear due to Him. If a single drop of zaqqum were dropped into the seas of this world, it would corrupt the livelihood of the people of the earth; so how about the one whose food it is?"

At-Tirmidhi, an-Nasa'i and Ibn Majah narrated it from the hadith of Shu'bah, and at-Tirmidhi said: Hasan sahih.

* *

As for His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Then indeed for them upon it is a mixture of boiling water﴾, Ibn 'Abbas said: it means drinking boiling water after the zaqqum.

In another narration from him: ﴿a mixture of boiling water﴾ means a mixing of boiling water.

Others said: it means that boiling water is mixed for them with pus and ghassaq, which flows from their private parts and eyes.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father related to us, Haywah ibn Shurayh al-Hadrami related to us, Baqiyyah ibn al-Walid related to us, from Safwan ibn 'Amr, ʿUbayd ibn Bisr informed me, from Abu Umamah al-Bahili, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, that he said: "Water is brought near to the people of the Fire, and they detest it; when it is brought close to him, it scorches his face, and the skin of his head falls into it. When he drinks it, it cuts his intestines until it comes out from his anus."

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father related to us, ʿAmr ibn Rafi' related to us, Ya'qub ibn 'Abdullah related to us, from Ja'far and Harun ibn 'Antarah, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr who said: When the people of the Fire become hungry, they cry out for help to the tree of zaqqum, and they eat from it, and it strips the skin of their faces off. If a passerby were to pass by them, he would recognize their faces by it. Then thirst is poured upon them, and they cry out for help and are given water like molten brass, which is water whose heat has reached its extreme. When they bring it near their mouths, the flesh of their faces, from which the skin has fallen, is roasted by its heat, and what is in their bellies is melted. Then they walk, their intestines flowing and their skins falling off. Then they are struck with iron maces, so that every limb falls in its place, and they cry out for destruction.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Then indeed their return is to Hellfire﴾, that is: after this separation, their return is to a Fire that blazes, a Blazing Hell and a Flaming Blaze, moving between this and that, as He said: ﴿They will circulate between it and scalding, boiling water﴾ [ar-Rahman: 44]. Thus Qatadah recited this verse at this point, and it is a good and strong interpretation.

As-Suddi said, in the reading of ʿAbdullah: "Then indeed their resting place is to Hellfire." ʿAbdullah used to say: By He in whose hand is my soul, on the Day of Resurrection the day will not reach midday until the people of Paradise have rested in Paradise and the people of the Fire have rested in the Fire. Then he recited: ﴿The companions of Paradise, that Day, will be better in residence and finer in resting place﴾ [al-Furqan: 24].

Ath-Thawri narrated from Maysarah, from al-Minhal ibn 'Amr, from Abu 'Ubaydah, from ʿAbdullah who said: The day will not reach midday on the Day of Resurrection until these rest and those rest. Sufyan said: I think he said, then he recited: ﴿The companions of Paradise, that Day, will be better in residence and finer in resting place﴾, then: ﴿Then indeed their resting place is to Hellfire.﴾

I say: According to this interpretation, "thumma" (then) is used to join one report to another report.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Indeed, they found their fathers astray﴾, that is: We only recompensed them with this because they found their fathers upon misguidance and followed them in it merely for that reason, without any proof or evidence. For this reason He said: ﴿So they are being rushed upon their footprints﴾. Mujahid said: [it means] like hastening at a run. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: they are being made to be foolish (or: led astray in haste).

The Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim) on surah 37, verses 71–74:

Allah (exalted is He) informs us about the earlier nations, that most of them were astray, setting up other gods alongside Allah. He (exalted is He) also mentions that He sent among them warners, who warned them of the might of Allah and cautioned them against His wrath and vengeance, those who disbelieved in Him and worshipped other than Him, and that they persisted in opposing their messengers and denying them. So He destroyed the deniers and annihilated them, and He saved the believers and granted them victory and triumph. For this reason He said: ﴿Then look at how was the end of those who were warned, except the sincere servants of Allah.﴾

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 37, verse 75–82:

He remained among them for a thousand years less fifty years. Allah became angry for his anger against them. Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn Abbas, saying: none remained except the descendants of Nuh, upon him be peace.

Ibn Kathir's commentary on Surah 37, verses 88–98:

Ibrahim (peace be upon him) only said that to his people so that he could stay behind in the town when they went out to their festival. He had been close to the time when they would leave for their festival, so he wanted to be alone with their gods in order to smash them. He said to them words that were true in reality, but they understood from them that he was sick according to what they believed. ﴿So they turned their backs and went away.﴾ Qatadah said: The Arabs say of someone who reflects, "He looked at the stars," meaning Qatadah's words: he looked at the sky, pondering what would distract them, and then said, ﴿Indeed, I am sick﴾, that is, weak.

As for the hadith that Ibn Jarir narrated here: Abu Kurayb told us, Abu Usamah told us, Hisham told me, from Muhammad, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Ibrahim (peace be upon him) never lied except three lies: two of them concerned the sake of Allah, his saying, ﴿Indeed, I am sick﴾, and his saying, ﴿Rather, it was their chief who did it﴾ [al-Anbiya: 63], and his saying about Sarah, 'She is my sister.'" (Tafsir al-Tabari 23/45; in al-Sunan al-Kubra, no. 8374, through Hammad ibn Usamah.) This hadith is recorded in the Sahihs and the Sunan through several chains. (It came through Ayyub from Muhammad ibn Sirin from Abu Hurayrah: al-Bukhari in his Sahih no. 5084 and Muslim in his Sahih no. 2371 through Jarir ibn Hazim; al-Bukhari in his Sahih no. 3358 through Hammad ibn Zayd. It also came through Abu al-Zinad from al-A'raj from Abu Hurayrah: al-Tirmidhi in his Sunan no. 3166 through Muhammad ibn Ishaq; al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan al-Kubra no. 8375 through Shu'ayb ibn Abi Hamzah.) However, this is not a case of an actual lie, which would be blameworthy for the one who commits it; far from it. The word "lie" was applied to it only figuratively. It was in fact an instance of al-ma'arid (indirect or allusive speech, i.e., saying something that is true in one sense while intending another) for a legitimate religious purpose, as in the hadith: "Indeed, in allusive speech (al-ma'arid) there is a sufficient alternative to lying." (Narrated by al-Bayhaqi in al-Sunan al-Kubra 10/199, through Dawud ibn al-Zabriqan from Sa'id from Qatadah from Zurarah from Imran ibn Husayn, marfu'. He also narrated it through Abd al-Wahhab ibn Ata from Sa'id from Qatadah from Mutarrif from Imran ibn al-Husayn, mawquf, and said: "This is the correct version, as a mawquf report.")

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated: My father told us, Ibn Abi Umar told us, Sufyan told us, from Ali ibn Zayd ibn Jud'an, from Abu Nadrah, from Abu Sa'id, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said concerning the three words of Ibrahim which he spoke: "Not one of them was spoken except to defend the religion of Allah, the Exalted. He said, ﴿Indeed, I am sick﴾; he said, ﴿Rather, it was their chief who did it﴾; and he said to the king when he wanted the woman, 'She is my sister.'" (Also narrated by al-Tirmidhi in al-Sunan no. 3148, from Ibn Abi Umar from Sufyan, in a long hadith about intercession. Al-Tirmidhi said: "This is a hasan sahih hadith." But Ali ibn Zayd ibn Jud'an is agreed by the imams to be weak.)

Sufyan said concerning His saying, ﴿Indeed, I am sick﴾: it means "afflicted by plague" (ta'in). They used to flee from one afflicted by plague, so he wanted to be alone with their gods. Al-Awfi narrated similarly from Ibn Abbas: ﴿Then he cast a glance at the stars, and said, "Indeed, I am sick."﴾ They said to him while he was in the house of their gods, "Come out!" He said, "I am afflicted by plague," so they left him, fearing the plague.

Qatadah said, narrating from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib: He saw a star that rose and said, ﴿Indeed, I am sick﴾. The Prophet of Allah was struggling with his people over his religion, ﴿so he said, "Indeed, I am sick."﴾

Others said: He said, ﴿Indeed, I am sick﴾ in reference to what was to come, meaning the sickness of death.

It was also said: He meant, ﴿Indeed, I am sick﴾, that is, sick at heart because of your worship of idols besides Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

Al-Hasan al-Basri said: The people of Ibrahim went out to their festival and urged him to go out with them. He lay down on his back and said, ﴿Indeed, I am sick﴾, and began looking at the sky. When they had gone out, he went to their gods and smashed them. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated this.

For this reason Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿So they turned their backs and went away﴾, that is, to their festival. ﴿Then he turned quickly to their gods﴾, that is, he went to them after they had left, swiftly and secretly. ﴿And said, "Will you not eat?"﴾ They had set food before the idols as an offering, hoping for blessing from them upon it.

Al-Suddi said: Ibrahim (peace be upon him) entered the house of the gods, and there they were in a great hall. Facing the entrance of the hall was a great idol, and beside it was another idol smaller than it. They were arranged side by side, each idol followed by one smaller than it, until they reached the doorway of the hall. They had placed food before the gods and said, "When we return, if the gods have blessed our food, we will eat it." When Ibrahim (peace be upon him) looked at the food set before them, he said, ﴿Will you not eat? What is the matter with you that you do not speak?﴾ As for His saying, ﴿Then he turned upon them, striking them with the right hand﴾, al-Farra' said: its meaning is "he inclined upon them, striking them with the right hand."

Qatadah and al-Jawhari said: ﴿He turned upon them, striking with the right hand﴾.

He struck them with the right hand because it is stronger and more effective. For this reason he left them in pieces, except a great one among them, so that they might come back to it, as the explanation of this was already given in Surah al-Anbiya.

His saying here: ﴿So they came hastening towards him﴾: Mujahid and others said: that is, they hurried.

This story is abbreviated here, and it is elaborated in Surah al-Anbiya. When they returned, they did not know at first who had done that, until they investigated and inquired, and they learned that Ibrahim (peace be upon him) was the one who had done it. When they came to rebuke him, he began to reproach and censure them, saying, ﴿Do you worship what you carve?﴾? That is: Do you worship, besides Allah, idols that you yourselves carve and make with your own hands? ﴿And Allah created you and what you make.﴾ The word "ma" may be a verbal-noun particle (masdariyyah), in which case the sense is: "Allah created you and your deeds." It may also mean "that which," in which case the sense is: "Allah created you and that which you make." Both interpretations are closely related, and the first is more apparent, because of what al-Bukhari narrated in his book Khalq Af'al al-'Ibad, from Ali ibn al-Madini, from Marwan ibn Mu'awiyah, from Abu Malik, from Rib'i ibn Hirash, from Hudhayfah, marfu': "Indeed Allah makes every maker and his making." (Khalq Af'al al-'Ibad, p. 73.) Some read it: ﴿And Allah created you and what you do.﴾

At that point, once the proof had been established against them, they resorted to seizing him by force and coercion. They said, ﴿Build for him a structure and throw him into the blazing fire.﴾ What happened to them is explained earlier in Surah al-Anbiya. Allah saved him from the fire and made him prevail over them, exalting his proof and granting it victory. For this reason Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿So they intended a scheme against him, but We made them the lowest.﴾

Ibn Kathir's commentary on Surah 37, verses 88–98:

Ibrahim (peace be upon him) only said that to his people so that he could stay behind in the town when they went out to their festival. He had been close to the time when they would leave for their festival, so he wanted to be alone with their gods in order to smash them. He said to them words that were true in reality, but they understood from them that he was sick according to what they believed. ﴿So they turned their backs and went away.﴾ Qatadah said: The Arabs say of someone who reflects, "He looked at the stars," meaning Qatadah's words: he looked at the sky, pondering what would distract them, and then said, ﴿Indeed, I am sick﴾, that is, weak.

As for the hadith that Ibn Jarir narrated here: Abu Kurayb told us, Abu Usamah told us, Hisham told me, from Muhammad, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Ibrahim (peace be upon him) never lied except three lies: two of them concerned the sake of Allah, his saying, ﴿Indeed, I am sick﴾, and his saying, ﴿Rather, it was their chief who did it﴾ [al-Anbiya: 63], and his saying about Sarah, 'She is my sister.'" (Tafsir al-Tabari 23/45; in al-Sunan al-Kubra, no. 8374, through Hammad ibn Usamah.) This hadith is recorded in the Sahihs and the Sunan through several chains. (It came through Ayyub from Muhammad ibn Sirin from Abu Hurayrah: al-Bukhari in his Sahih no. 5084 and Muslim in his Sahih no. 2371 through Jarir ibn Hazim; al-Bukhari in his Sahih no. 3358 through Hammad ibn Zayd. It also came through Abu al-Zinad from al-A'raj from Abu Hurayrah: al-Tirmidhi in his Sunan no. 3166 through Muhammad ibn Ishaq; al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan al-Kubra no. 8375 through Shu'ayb ibn Abi Hamzah.) However, this is not a case of an actual lie, which would be blameworthy for the one who commits it; far from it. The word "lie" was applied to it only figuratively. It was in fact an instance of al-ma'arid (indirect or allusive speech, i.e., saying something that is true in one sense while intending another) for a legitimate religious purpose, as in the hadith: "Indeed, in allusive speech (al-ma'arid) there is a sufficient alternative to lying." (Narrated by al-Bayhaqi in al-Sunan al-Kubra 10/199, through Dawud ibn al-Zabriqan from Sa'id from Qatadah from Zurarah from Imran ibn Husayn, marfu'. He also narrated it through Abd al-Wahhab ibn Ata from Sa'id from Qatadah from Mutarrif from Imran ibn al-Husayn, mawquf, and said: "This is the correct version, as a mawquf report.")

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated: My father told us, Ibn Abi Umar told us, Sufyan told us, from Ali ibn Zayd ibn Jud'an, from Abu Nadrah, from Abu Sa'id, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said concerning the three words of Ibrahim which he spoke: "Not one of them was spoken except to defend the religion of Allah, the Exalted. He said, ﴿Indeed, I am sick﴾; he said, ﴿Rather, it was their chief who did it﴾; and he said to the king when he wanted the woman, 'She is my sister.'" (Also narrated by al-Tirmidhi in al-Sunan no. 3148, from Ibn Abi Umar from Sufyan, in a long hadith about intercession. Al-Tirmidhi said: "This is a hasan sahih hadith." But Ali ibn Zayd ibn Jud'an is agreed by the imams to be weak.)

Sufyan said concerning His saying, ﴿Indeed, I am sick﴾: it means "afflicted by plague" (ta'in). They used to flee from one afflicted by plague, so he wanted to be alone with their gods. Al-Awfi narrated similarly from Ibn Abbas: ﴿Then he cast a glance at the stars, and said, "Indeed, I am sick."﴾ They said to him while he was in the house of their gods, "Come out!" He said, "I am afflicted by plague," so they left him, fearing the plague.

Qatadah said, narrating from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib: He saw a star that rose and said, ﴿Indeed, I am sick﴾. The Prophet of Allah was struggling with his people over his religion, ﴿so he said, "Indeed, I am sick."﴾

Others said: He said, ﴿Indeed, I am sick﴾ in reference to what was to come, meaning the sickness of death.

It was also said: He meant, ﴿Indeed, I am sick﴾, that is, sick at heart because of your worship of idols besides Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

Al-Hasan al-Basri said: The people of Ibrahim went out to their festival and urged him to go out with them. He lay down on his back and said, ﴿Indeed, I am sick﴾, and began looking at the sky. When they had gone out, he went to their gods and smashed them. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated this.

For this reason Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿So they turned their backs and went away﴾, that is, to their festival. ﴿Then he turned quickly to their gods﴾, that is, he went to them after they had left, swiftly and secretly. ﴿And said, "Will you not eat?"﴾ They had set food before the idols as an offering, hoping for blessing from them upon it.

Al-Suddi said: Ibrahim (peace be upon him) entered the house of the gods, and there they were in a great hall. Facing the entrance of the hall was a great idol, and beside it was another idol smaller than it. They were arranged side by side, each idol followed by one smaller than it, until they reached the doorway of the hall. They had placed food before the gods and said, "When we return, if the gods have blessed our food, we will eat it." When Ibrahim (peace be upon him) looked at the food set before them, he said, ﴿Will you not eat? What is the matter with you that you do not speak?﴾ As for His saying, ﴿Then he turned upon them, striking them with the right hand﴾, al-Farra' said: its meaning is "he inclined upon them, striking them with the right hand."

Qatadah and al-Jawhari said: ﴿He turned upon them, striking with the right hand﴾.

He struck them with the right hand because it is stronger and more effective. For this reason he left them in pieces, except a great one among them, so that they might come back to it, as the explanation of this was already given in Surah al-Anbiya.

Allah, exalted is He, says, informing about His friend Ibrahim (peace be upon him) [addition from manuscripts T and S]: After Allah had given him victory over his people, and after he had despaired of their faith having witnessed the great signs, he emigrated from among them and said: ﴿Indeed, I am going to my Lord; He will guide me. My Lord, grant me [a child] from among the righteous.﴾ That is, he asked for obedient children as a replacement for his people and kindred whom he had left. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿So We gave him good tidings of a forbearing boy.﴾ This boy was Isma'il (peace be upon him), for he was the first son whose birth Ibrahim (peace be upon him) was given good tidings of. He was older than Ishaq by the consensus of the Muslims and the People of the Book. Indeed, in the text of their own scripture it is stated that Isma'il was born to Ibrahim (peace be upon him) when he was eighty-six years old, and that Ishaq was born when Ibrahim was ninety-nine years old. According to them, Allah commanded Ibrahim to sacrifice his son, his only son, and in one version, "his firstborn." So they inserted here, falsely and with slander, "Ishaq." This is not permissible, because it contradicts the text of their scripture. They inserted "Ishaq" only because he is their father, whereas Isma'il is the father of the Arabs, so they envied them. They added to it and distorted the word "only son" (wahid), giving it the meaning of "the one who has no other," since Isma'il had been taken by his father, together with his mother, to the area beside Makkah. This is a false interpretation and a baseless distortion, for the word "wahid" is only used of one who has no other. Moreover, the firstborn son has a distinction that later sons do not have, so the command to sacrifice him is more emphatic as a trial and test.

A group of scholars held that the one sacrificed was Ishaq. This view is attributed to a group of the early generations (al-salaf), and it is even reported from some of the Companions (al-Sahabah). But it is not found in the Book or the Sunnah. I do not think this view was taken except from the rabbis of the People of the Book, and it was accepted as settled without evidence. The Book of Allah bears witness to and guides toward its being Isma'il, for it mentions the good tidings of the forbearing boy and mentions that he is the one to be sacrificed. Then after that He said: ﴿And We gave him good tidings of Ishaq, a prophet from among the righteous.﴾ When the angels gave Ibrahim good tidings of Ishaq, they said: ﴿Indeed, we give you good tidings of a knowing boy.﴾ [al-Hijr: 53] And He said: ﴿So We gave her good tidings of Ishaq, and after Ishaq, Ya'qub.﴾ [Hud: 71] That is, a son named Ya'qub would be born to him during the lifetime of both of them, and from his offspring would come descendants and progeny. We have already mentioned there that after this promise it is not permissible that he be commanded to sacrifice him while still a child, because Allah [the Exalted] [addition in manuscript T] had promised both of them that he would have descendants and that there would be progeny for him. How, then, could he be commanded to sacrifice him as a child after this? Isma'il is described here as forbearing because that suits this situation.

* *

His saying: ﴿When he reached the age of exertion with him⟩ means: he grew up, became strong, and began to walk with his father and go about with him. Ibrahim (peace be upon him) used to go at all times to check on his son and the son's mother in the land of Faran, and to look into their affairs. It has been mentioned that he would ride swiftly to that place on the Buraq. But Allah knows best.

It is reported from Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, Ikrimah, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, 'Ata al-Khurasani, Zayd ibn Aslam, and others: ﴿When he reached the age of exertion with him⟩ means: he grew up, became capable, and was able to do what his father did of striving and working. ﴿When he reached the age of exertion with him, he said: "O my son, indeed I see in a dream that I am sacrificing you, so see what you think."⟩ 'Ubayd ibn 'Umayr said: The dreams of the prophets are revelation. Then he recited this verse: ﴿He said, "O my son, indeed I see in a dream that I am sacrificing you, so see what you think."⟩

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated to us: 'Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn al-Junayd narrated to us, Abu 'Abd al-Malik al-Karandi narrated to us, Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah narrated to us, from Isra'il ibn Yunus, from Simak, from Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The dreams of the prophets in sleep are revelation." This is not in any of the Six Books by this route. [Al-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (12/6) narrated it by another route from Simak: he narrated it through al-Firyabi, from Sufyan, from Simak ibn Harb, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas.]

He informed his son of this only so that it would be easier for him, and to test his patience, endurance, and resolve from his youth in obeying Allah the Exalted and obeying his father.

﴿He said, "O my father, do what you are commanded."⟩ That is: carry out what Allah has commanded you regarding my slaughter. ﴿"You will find me, if Allah wills, among the patient."⟩ That is: I will be patient and will seek reward for that with Allah, Mighty and Majestic. He spoke the truth, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him, in what he promised. For this reason Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And mention in the Book Isma'il. Indeed, he was true to his promise, and he was a messenger and a prophet. And he used to enjoin on his people prayer and zakah, and he was pleasing to his Lord.⟩ [Maryam: 54–55]

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿So when they both submitted and he put him down upon his forehead⟩ means: when both of them bore witness [to the faith] and remembered Allah the Exalted, Ibrahim [prepared] for the slaughter, and the son [prepared] for the witness of death. It is also said: ﴿aslama﴾ [in the sense] of [yastaslima] and yanqada: they surrendered and submitted. Ibrahim complied with Allah's command, and Isma'il obeyed Allah and his father. This was said by Mujahid, Ikrimah, al-Suddi, Qatadah, Ibn Ishaq, and others.

The meaning of ﴿and he put him down upon his forehead⟩ is that he threw him onto his face so that he could slaughter him from the nape of his neck, and so that he would not see his face at the time of slaughter, to make it easier for him. Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, al-Dahhak, and Qatadah said: ﴿and he put him down upon his forehead⟩ means: he laid him down on his face.

Imam Ahmad said: Surayj [in manuscript A: Shurayj] and Yunus narrated to us, both saying: Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, from Abu 'Asim al-Ghanawi, from Abu al-Tufayl [in manuscript T: "with its chain"], from Ibn 'Abbas, that he said: When Ibrahim was commanded with the rites (al-manasik) [in manuscript A: "When Allah commanded Ibrahim (peace be upon him) with the rites"], Satan confronted him at the place of running (al-sa'y), so he raced him, and Ibrahim outran him. Then Jibril took him to Jamrat al-'Aqabah, and Satan confronted him there, so he pelted him with seven pebbles until he departed. Then he confronted him at the middle jamrah, and he pelted him with seven pebbles. Then he laid him down upon his forehead, and Isma'il was wearing a white shirt. He said to him: "O father, I have no garment to be shrouded in except this one, so take it off so that you may shroud me in it." He began to take it off, and he was called from behind: ﴿"O Ibrahim, you have fulfilled the vision."⟩ Ibrahim turned, and behold, there was a white ram with curled horns and beautiful eyes. Ibn 'Abbas said: We used to follow that kind of ram.

He mentioned the complete hadith at length in "al-Manasik." [al-Musnad (1/297)] Then Ahmad narrated it at length from Yunus, from Hammad ibn Salamah, from 'Ata ibn al-Sa'ib, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr [in manuscript T: "with its chain"], from Ibn 'Abbas, and he mentioned something similar, except that he said: "Ishaq." [al-Musnad (1/306)] So there are two reports from Ibn 'Abbas regarding the identity of the one to be sacrificed, and the more apparent from him is Isma'il, for reasons that will come later.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said, from al-Hasan ibn Dinar, from Qatadah, from Ja'far ibn Iyas, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿And We ransomed him with a great sacrifice.⟩ He said: A ram came out to him from Paradise, which had grazed for forty autumns before that. Ibrahim sent his son away and followed the ram, and it led him to the first jamrah, and he pelted it with seven pebbles, and it escaped from him there. It came to the middle jamrah, and he brought it out there, and he pelted it with seven pebbles, and then it escaped. He caught up with it at the greatest jamrah, and he pelted it with seven pebbles, and brought it out there. Then he took it and brought it to the place of sacrifice (al-manhar) at Mina, and slaughtered it. By Him in whose hand is the soul of Ibn 'Abbas, the head of the ram was indeed hanging by its horns on the gutter of the Ka'bah from the beginning of Islam, and it had dried out, meaning: it had become dry.

'Abd al-Razzaq said: Ma'mar informed us, from al-Zuhri, who informed us, al-Qasim said: Abu Hurayrah and Ka'b met. Abu Hurayrah began to narrate from the Prophet (ﷺ), and Ka'b began to narrate from the scriptures. Abu Hurayrah said: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Every prophet has a supplication that is answered, and I have kept my supplication as an intercession for my nation on the Day of Resurrection." Ka'b said to him: "Did you hear this from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)?" He said: "Yes." He said: "May my father and mother be your ransom, or: may his father and mother be his ransom. Shall I not tell you about Ibrahim (peace be upon him)? When he was shown the sacrifice of his son Ishaq, Satan said: 'If I do not tempt these people at this [moment], I will never tempt them.' So Ibrahim went out with his son to sacrifice him. Satan went and entered upon Sarah and said: 'Where did Ibrahim take your son?' She said: 'He went out with him for some need of his.' He said: 'He did not go out for a need; he took him only to sacrifice him.' She said: 'And why would he sacrifice him?' He said: 'He claims that his Lord commanded him to do so.' She said: 'Then he has done well to obey his Lord.' Satan went after the two of them and said to the boy: 'Where is your father taking you?' He said: 'For some need of his.' He said: 'He does not take you for a need; he takes you only to sacrifice you.' He said: 'And why would he sacrifice me?' He said: 'He claims that his Lord commanded him to do so.' He said: 'By Allah, if Allah has commanded him to do so, then he will certainly do it.' So he despaired of him, and he left him and caught up with Ibrahim, and said: 'Where did you go out with your son?' He said: 'For a need.' He said: 'You did not go out with him for a need; you went out with him only to sacrifice him.' He said: 'And why would I sacrifice him?' He said: 'You claim that your Lord commanded you to do so.' He said: 'By Allah, if my Lord has commanded me to do so, I will certainly do it.' So he left him and despaired of being obeyed."

Ibn Jarir narrated it from Yunus, from Ibn Wahb, from Yunus ibn Yazid, from Ibn Shihab, that 'Amr ibn Abi Sufyan ibn Usayd [in manuscript A: "Asad"] ibn Jariyah al-Thaqafi informed him that Ka'b said to Abu Hurayrah ... and he mentioned it at length, and at its end he said: Allah revealed to Ishaq: "I have given you a supplication, and I will answer you in it." Ishaq said: "O Allah, I ask You to accept from me: any servant who meets You from among the first and the last, who does not associate anything with You, admit him into Paradise."

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated to us: My father narrated to us, Muhammad ibn al-Wazir al-Dimashqi narrated to us, al-Walid ibn Muslim narrated to us, 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam narrated to us, from his father, from 'Ata ibn Yasar [in manuscript T: "and he narrated with his chain"], from Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him) [addition from manuscript T], who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah gave me the choice between forgiving half of my nation and between my keeping my intercession hidden. So I hid my intercession, and I hoped that it would be [an expiation] for my nation as a whole [in manuscript A: 'that it would be more general']. And had it not been for what the righteous servant (Ibrahim) had preceded me in, I would have hastened my supplication for it. Indeed, when Allah relieved Ishaq of the distress of the slaughter, it was said to him: 'O Ishaq, ask, and you will be given.' He said: 'As for Him in whose hand is my soul, I will hasten it before the whisperings of Satan. O Allah, whoever dies without associating anything with You, forgive him and admit him into Paradise.'"

This is a hadith, a strange and rejected (munkar) narration, narrated by al-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Awsat (no. 3603) and by Ibn 'Adi in al-Kamil (4/272) through al-Walid ibn Muslim, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam, with it. Ibn Abi Hatim also mentioned it in al-'Ilal (2/219) and said: "I asked my father, and he said: 'This is a munkar hadith.'" 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam is weak in narration. I fear that there is an interpolated addition (mudraja) in the hadith, namely his saying: "Indeed Allah, when He relieved Ishaq..." to the end. And Allah knows best. So if this is preserved, the more likely reading is that the context is about Isma'il, and they distorted it to Ishaq out of envy, as has already been mentioned. Otherwise, the rites of pilgrimage and the sacrifices are only located at Mina, in the land of Makkah, where Isma'il, not Ishaq, was [peace be upon them both]. Ishaq was in the land of Canaan in the region of the Levant.

* *

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And We called to him, "O Abraham, you have fulfilled the vision."﴾ That is: the purpose of your vision has been achieved by your laying your son down for slaughter.

Al-Suddi and others mentioned that he drew the knife across his neck, but it did not cut anything; rather, a plate of copper came between the knife and him. Then Ibrahim, peace be upon him, was called at that moment: ﴿You have fulfilled the vision.﴾

* *

And His saying: ﴿Indeed, thus do We reward the doers of good.﴾ That is: thus do We turn away from those who obey Us hardships and calamities, and We make for them, in their affair, relief and a way out, as in His saying the Exalted: ﴿And whoever fears Allah, He will make for him a way out, and will provide for him from where he does not expect. And whoever relies upon Allah, then He is sufficient for him. Indeed, Allah will accomplish His purpose. Allah has already set for everything a decree.﴾ [At-Talaq: 2-3]

A group of scholars of legal theory (usul al-fiqh) used this verse and the story as evidence for the validity of naskh (abrogation, the lifting of a previously prescribed ruling by a later one) before the command could be carried out, contrary to a group of the Mu'tazilah (a rationalist theological school). The proof from this is clear: Allah the Exalted prescribed for Ibrahim the slaughter of his son, then abrogated it for him and turned it into a ransom. The primary purpose of the original command was to reward the Friend (Khalil) for his patience in the face of slaughtering his son and his determination to do so. For this reason Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, this is the clear trial.﴾ That is: the evident and manifest test, in that he was commanded to slaughter his son, and he hastened to that, submitting to the command of Allah and obeying Him. For this reason Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And Abraham who fulfilled [his covenant].﴾ [An-Najm: 37]

* *

And His saying: ﴿And We ransomed him with a great sacrifice.﴾ Sufyan al-Thawri narrated from Jabir al-Ju'fi, from Abu al-Tufayl, from 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, regarding ﴿And We ransomed him with a great sacrifice﴾: he said: "With a white ram, with beautiful eyes and curved horns, which had been tied to a samurah tree." Abu al-Tufayl said: "They found it tied to a samurah tree on Thabir."

Al-Thawri also said, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Uthman ibn Khuthaym, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "A ram that had grazed in Paradise for forty autumns."

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Yusuf ibn Ya'qub al-Saffar narrated to us, Dawud al-'Attar narrated to us, from Ibn Khuthaym, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "The rock that is in Mina at the base of Thabir is the rock on which Ibrahim slaughtered the ransom for his son. There descended upon it from Thabir a ram, with beautiful eyes and curved horns, which bleated; so he slaughtered it. It is the ram that Adam's son (Qabil/Habil) offered, and it was accepted from him. It was kept stored until Ishaq was ransomed with it."

It is also narrated from Sa'id ibn Jubayr that he said: "The ram used to graze in Paradise until Thabir split open for it, and it had red wool on it."

From al-Hasan al-Basri: the name of Ibrahim's ram was Jarir.

Ibn Jurayj said: 'Ubayd ibn 'Umayr said: "He slaughtered it at al-Maqam." Mujahid said: "He slaughtered it at Mina, at the place of sacrifice (al-mantar)." Hushaym narrated from Sayyar, from 'Ikrimah, that Ibn 'Abbas once issued a fatwa to the one who had vowed to sacrifice himself, instructing him to sacrifice one hundred camels. Then he said afterwards: "Had I issued him a fatwa to sacrifice a ram, it would have sufficed him to slaughter a ram, for Allah the Exalted said in His Book: ﴿And We ransomed him with a great sacrifice.﴾" The sound view, which most scholars hold, is that he was ransomed with a ram. Al-Thawri narrated from a man, from Abu Salih, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿And We ransomed him with a great sacrifice﴾: he said: "A wa'l (a mountain goat)."

Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated from 'Amr ibn 'Ubayd, from al-Hasan, that he used to say: "Isma'il was ransomed only with a male antelope (tays min al-aruwa), which descended upon him from Thabir."

Imam Ahmad has also said: Sufyan narrated to us, Mansur narrated to us, from his maternal uncle Musafi', from Safiyyah bint Shaybah, who said: "A woman from the Banu Sulaym, who had given birth to most of the people of our household, informed me that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent for 'Uthman ibn Talhah" (and at one point she said: "She asked 'Uthman: 'Why did the Prophet ﷺ call you?' He said: 'He said: "I had seen the two horns of the ram when I entered the House, and I forgot to order you to cover them. So cover them, for it is not fitting that there be anything in the House that distracts the one who prays."'") Sufyan said: "The two horns of the ram remained hanging in the House until the House burned, and they burned." [Al-Musnad (4/68)]

This is independent evidence that it was Isma'il, peace be upon him, for the Quraysh inherited the two horns of the ram with which Ibrahim was ransomed, from predecessor to successor, generation after generation, until Allah sent His Messenger ﷺ.

A section on the narrations transmitted from the early generations (al-salaf) regarding who the sacrificed son was:

Mention of those who said: it was Ishaq [peace be upon him]:

Hamzah al-Zayyat narrated from Abu Maysarah, may Allah have mercy on him, who said: Yusuf, peace be upon him, said to the king to his face: "Do you desire to eat with me? I am—by Allah—Yusuf ibn Ya'qub, the Prophet of Allah, son of Ishaq, the one who was sacrificed by Allah, son of Ibrahim, the Friend of Allah."

Al-Thawri said, from Abu Sinan, from Ibn Abi al-Hudhayl: that Yusuf, peace be upon him, said the same to the king.

Sufyan al-Thawri said, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Ubayd ibn 'Umayr, from his father, who said: "Musa said: 'O Lord, they say: "O God of Ibrahim, Ishaq and Ya'qub." Why do they say that?' He said: 'Ibrahim never once preferred anything over Me without My choosing him over it. As for Ishaq, he gave himself to Me for slaughter, and he was more generous than that. As for Ya'qub, whenever I increased him in trial, he increased in good opinion of Me.'"

Shu'bah said, from Abu Ishaq, from Abu al-Ahwas, who said: A man boasted in the presence of Ibn Mas'ud, saying: "I am so-and-so son of so-and-so, the son of noble elders." 'Abd Allah said: "That is Yusuf ibn Ya'qub ibn Ishaq, the one sacrificed by Allah, son of Ibrahim, the Friend of Allah [may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon them all]."

This is sound up to Ibn Mas'ud. Likewise, 'Ikrimah narrated from Ibn 'Abbas that it was Ishaq, and from his father al-'Abbas and from 'Ali ibn Abi Talib the same. Likewise said 'Ikrimah, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Mujahid, al-Sha'bi, 'Ubayd ibn 'Umayr, Abu Maysarah, Zayd ibn Aslam, 'Abd Allah ibn Shaqiq, al-Zuhri, al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazzah, Makhul, 'Uthman ibn Hadir, al-Suddi, al-Hasan, Qatadah, Abu al-Hudhayl, and Ibn Sabit. This is the view chosen by Ibn Jarir. His narration from Ka'b al-Ahbar that it was Ishaq has already been mentioned.

Thus Ibn Ishaq narrated from 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Bakr, from al-Zuhri, from Abu Sufyan ibn al-'Ala', ibn Jariyah, from Abu Hurayrah, from Ka'b al-Ahbar, that he said: "It was Ishaq." [Narrated by al-Tabari in his tafsir (23/52)]

And all of these reports, and Allah knows best, derive from Ka'b al-Ahbar. For when he embraced Islam during the caliphate of 'Umar, he began to narrate to 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, from his books. 'Umar would sometimes listen to him, so people became lenient about listening to what he had, and they transmitted from him both its worthless and its valuable parts, while this Ummah—and Allah knows best—has no need for a single letter of what he had. Al-Baghawi has recorded this view, that it was Ishaq, from 'Umar, 'Ali, Ibn Mas'ud, and al-'Abbas, and from the Successors (tabi'un): Ka'b al-Ahbar, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Qatadah, Masruq, 'Ikrimah, Muqatil, 'Ata', al-Zuhri, and al-Suddi. He said: "And it is one of the two reports from Ibn 'Abbas." [Ma'alim al-Tanzil of al-Baghawi (7/46)]

A hadith has been transmitted on this subject—if it were established, we would act upon it wholeheartedly, but its chain is not sound. Ibn Jarir said:

Abu Kurayb narrated to us, Zayd ibn Hubab narrated to us, from al-Hasan ibn Dinar, from 'Ali ibn Zayd ibn Jud'an, from al-Hasan, from al-Ahnaf ibn Qays, from al-'Abbas ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib, from the Prophet ﷺ, in a hadith he mentioned, who said: "He was Ishaq." [Tafsir al-Tabari (23/52)]
