وَأَمَرَ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى حُوتًا مِنَ الْبَحْرِ الْأَخْضَرِ أَنْ يَشُقَّ الْبِحَارَ، وَأَنْ يَلْتَقِمَ يُونُسَ، عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ، فَلَا يَهْشِمُ لَهُ لَحْمًا، وَلَا يَكْسِرَ لَهُ عَظْمًا. فَجَاءَ ذَلِكَ الْحُوتُ وَأَلْقَى يُونُسُ، عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ، نَفْسَهُ فَالْتَقَمَهُ الْحُوتُ وَذَهَبَ بِهِ فَطَافَ بِهِ الْبِحَارَ كُلَّهَا. وَلَمَّا اسْتَقَرَّ يُونُسُ فِي بَطْنِ الْحُوتِ، حَسِبَ أَنَّهُ قَدْ مَاتَ، ثُمَّ حَرَّكَ رَأْسَهُ وَرِجْلَيْهِ وَأَطْرَافَهُ فَإِذَا هُوَ حَيٌّ، فَقَامَ يُصَلِّي فِي بَطْنِ الْحُوتِ، وَكَانَ مِنْ جُمْلَةِ دُعَائِهِ: "يَا رَبِّ، اتَّخَذْتُ لَكَ مَسْجِدًا فِي مَوْضِعٍ لَمْ يَبْلُغْهُ أَحَدٌ مِنَ النَّاسِ". وَاخْتَلَفُوا فِي مِقْدَارِ مَا لَبِثَ فِي بَطْنِ الْحُوتِ، فَقِيلَ: ثَلَاثَةَ أَيَّامٍ، قَالَهُ قَتَادَةُ. وَقِيلَ: سَبْعَةَ أَيَّامٍ، قَالَهُ جَعْفَرُ الصَّادِقُ. وَقِيلَ: أَرْبَعِينَ يَوْمًا، قَالَهُ أَبُو مَالِكٍ.

وَقَالَ مُجَالِدٌ، عَنِ الشَّعْبِيِّ: الْتَقَمَهُ ضُحًى، وَقَذَفَهُ عَشِيَّةً.

وَاللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ بِمِقْدَارِ ذَلِكَ. وَفِي شِعْرِ أُمَيَّةَ بْنِ أَبِي الصَّلْتِ:

وَأَنْتَ بِفَضْلٍ مِنْكَ نَجَّيْتَ يُونُسًا ... وَقَدْ بَاتَ فِي أَضْعَافِ حُوتٍ لَيَالِيَا

[[The verse is in Ibn Hisham's al-Sirah al-Nabawiyyah (1/228).]]

* *

وَقَوْلُهُ: ﴿فَلَوْلا أَنَّهُ كَانَ مِنَ الْمُسَبِّحِينَ لَلَبِثَ فِي بَطْنِهِ إِلَى يَوْمِ يُبْعَثُونَ﴾ قِيلَ: لَوْلَا مَا تَقَدَّمَ لَهُ مِنَ الْعَمَلِ فِي الرَّخَاءِ. قَالَهُ الضَّحَّاكُ بْنُ قَيْسٍ، وَأَبُو الْعَالِيَةِ، وَوَهْبُ بْنُ مُنَبِّهٍ، وَقَتَادَةُ، وَغَيْرُ وَاحِدٍ. وَاخْتَارَهُ ابْنُ جَرِيرٍ. وَقَدْ وَرَدَ فِي الْحَدِيثِ الَّذِي سَنُورِدُهُ مَا يَدُلُّ عَلَى ذَلِكَ إِنْ صَحَّ الْخَبَرُ. وَفِي حَدِيثٍ عَنِ ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ: "تَعَرَّفْ إِلَى اللَّهِ فِي الرَّخَاءِ يَعْرِفْكَ فِي الشِّدَّةِ". [[Its takhrij will come under verse 38 of Surah al-Zumar.]]

وَقَالَ ابْنُ عَبَّاسٍ، وَسَعِيدُ بْنُ جُبَيْرٍ، وَالضَّحَّاكُ، وَعَطَاءُ بْنُ السَّائِبِ، وَالسُّدِّيُّ، وَالْحَسَنُ، وَقَتَادَةُ: ﴿فَلَوْلا أَنَّهُ كَانَ مِنَ الْمُسَبِّحِينَ﴾ يَعْنِي: الْمُصَلِّينَ.

وَصَرَّحَ بَعْضُهُمْ بِأَنَّهُ كَانَ مِنَ الْمُصَلِّينَ قَبْلَ ذَلِكَ. وَقَالَ بَعْضُهُمْ: كَانَ مِنَ الْمُسَبِّحِينَ فِي جَوْفِ أَبَوَيْهِ. وَقِيلَ: الْمُرَادُ بِقَوْلِهِ: ﴿فَلَوْلا أَنَّهُ كَانَ مِنَ الْمُسَبِّحِينَ﴾ هُوَ قَوْلُهُ: ﴿فَنَادَى فِي الظُّلُمَاتِ أَنْ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا أَنْتَ سُبْحَانَكَ إِنِّي كُنْتُ مِنَ الظَّالِمِينَ فَاسْتَجَبْنَا لَهُ وَنَجَّيْنَاهُ مِنَ الْغَمِّ وَكَذَلِكَ نُنْجِي الْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ [الأنبياء: 87، 88]. قَالَهُ سَعِيدُ بْنُ جُبَيْرٍ وَغَيْرُهُ.

وَقَالَ ابْنُ أَبِي حَاتِمٍ: حَدَّثَنَا أَبُو عُبَيْدِ اللَّهِ ابْنُ أَخِي ابْنِ وَهْبٍ، حَدَّثَنَا عَمِّي، حَدَّثَنَا أَبُو صَخْرٍ: أَنَّ يَزِيدَ الرَّقَاشِيَّ حَدَّثَهُ: أَنَّهُ سَمِعَ أَنَسَ بْنَ مَالِكٍ -وَلَا أَعْلَمُ إِلَّا أَنَّ أَنَسًا يَرْفَعُ الْحَدِيثَ إِلَى رَسُولِ اللَّهِ ﷺ- "أَنَّ يُونُسَ النَّبِيَّ ﷺ حِينَ بَدَا لَهُ أَنْ يَدْعُوَ بِهَذِهِ الْكَلِمَاتِ، وَهُوَ فِي بَطْنِ الْحُوتِ، فَقَالَ: اللَّهُمَّ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا أَنْتَ سُبْحَانَكَ إِنِّي كُنْتُ مِنَ الظَّالِمِينَ. فَأَقْبَلَتِ الدَّعْوَةُ تَحُفُّ بِالْعَرْشِ، قَالَتِ الْمَلَائِكَةُ: يَا رَبِّ، هَذَا صَوْتٌ ضَعِيفٌ مَعْرُوفٌ مِنْ بِلَادٍ بَعِيدَةٍ غَرِيبَةٍ؟ فَقَالَ: أَمَا تَعْرِفُونَ ذَلِكَ؟ قَالُوا: يَا رَبِّ، وَمَنْ هُوَ؟ قَالَ: عَبْدِي يُونُسُ. قَالُوا: عَبْدُكَ يُونُسُ الَّذِي لَمْ يَزَلْ يُرْفَعُ لَهُ عَمَلٌ مُتَقَبَّلٌ، وَدَعْوَةٌ مُسْتَجَابَةٌ؟ قَالُوا: يَا رَبِّ، أَوَلَا تَرْحَمُ مَا كَانَ يَصْنَعُ فِي الرَّخَاءِ فَتُنَجِّيهِ فِي الْبَلَاءِ؟ قَالَ: بَلَى. فَأَمَرَ الْحُوتَ فَطَرَحَهُ بِالْعَرَاءِ".

وَرَوَاهُ ابْنُ جَرِيرٍ، عَنْ يُونُسَ، عَنِ ابْنِ وَهْبٍ، بِهِ. [[Blank space in MS. S.]] [[Tafsir al-Tabari (23/64).]] زَادَ ابْنُ أَبِي حَاتِمٍ: قَالَ أَبُو صَخْرٍ حُمَيْدُ بْنُ زِيَادٍ: فَأَخْبَرَنِي ابْنُ قُسَيْطٍ وَأَنَا أُحَدِّثُهُ هَذَا الْحَدِيثَ: أَنَّهُ سَمِعَ أَبَا هُرَيْرَةَ يَقُولُ: "طُرِحَ بِالْعَرَاءِ، وَأَنْبَتَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ الْيَقْطِينَةَ". قُلْنَا: يَا أَبَا هُرَيْرَةَ، وَمَا الْيَقْطِينَةُ؟ قَالَ: شَجَرَةُ الدُّبَّاءِ. قَالَ أَبُو هُرَيْرَةَ: وَهَيَّأَ اللَّهُ لَهُ أَرْوِيَّةً وَحْشِيَّةً تَأْكُلُ مِنْ خَشَاشِ الْأَرْضِ -أَوْ قَالَ: هَشَاشِ الْأَرْضِ- قَالَ: فَتَتَفَشَّخُ عَلَيْهِ فَتَرْوِيهِ مِنْ لَبَنِهَا كُلَّ عَشِيَّةٍ وَبُكْرَةٍ حَتَّى نَبَتَ.

وَقَالَ أُمَيَّةُ بْنُ أَبِي الصَّلْتِ فِي ذَلِكَ بَيْتًا مِنْ شِعْرِهِ:

فَأَنْبَتَ يَقْطِينًا عَلَيْهِ بِرَحْمَةٍ ... مِنَ اللَّهِ لَوْلَا اللَّهُ أُلْفِيَ ضَاحِيَا

[[The verse is in Ibn Hisham's al-Sirah al-Nabawiyyah (1/228).]]

وَقَدْ تَقَدَّمَ حَدِيثُ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ مُسْنَدًا مَرْفُوعًا فِي تَفْسِيرِ سُورَةِ "الْأَنْبِيَاءِ". [[Surah al-Anbiya', verse 87.]]

وَلِهَذَا قَالَ تَعَالَى: ﴿فَنَبَذْنَاهُ﴾ أَيْ: أَلْقَيْنَاهُ ﴿بِالْعَرَاءِ﴾. قَالَ ابْنُ عَبَّاسٍ وَغَيْرُهُ: وَهِيَ الْأَرْضُ الَّتِي لَيْسَ بِهَا نَبْتٌ وَلَا بِنَاءٌ. قِيلَ: عَلَى جَانِبِ دِجْلَةَ. وَقِيلَ: بِأَرْضِ الْيَمَنِ. فَاللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ.

﴿وَهُوَ سَقِيمٌ﴾ أَيْ: ضَعِيفُ الْبَدَنِ. قَالَ ابْنُ مَسْعُودٍ، رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ: كَهَيْئَةِ الْفَرْخِ لَيْسَ عَلَيْهِ رِيشٌ. وَقَالَ السُّدِّيُّ: كَهَيْئَةِ الصَّبِيِّ حِينَ يُولَدُ، وَهُوَ الْمَنْفُوسُ. وَقَالَهُ ابْنُ عَبَّاسٍ، وَابْنُ زَيْدٍ أَيْضًا.

﴿وَأَنْبَتْنَا عَلَيْهِ شَجَرَةً مِنْ يَقْطِينٍ﴾. قَالَ ابْنُ مَسْعُودٍ، وَابْنُ عَبَّاسٍ، وَمُجَاهِدٌ، وَعِكْرِمَةُ، وَسَعِيدُ بْنُ جُبَيْرٍ، وَوَهْبُ بْنُ مُنَبِّهٍ، وَهِلَالُ بْنُ يَسَافٍ، وَعَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ طَاوُسٍ، وَالسُّدِّيُّ، وَقَتَادَةُ، وَالضَّحَّاكُ، وَعَطَاءٌ الْخُرَاسَانِيُّ، وَغَيْرُ وَاحِدٍ، قَالُوا كُلُّهُمْ: الْيَقْطِينُ هُوَ الْقَرْعُ.

وَقَالَ هُشَيْمٌ، عَنِ الْقَاسِمِ بْنِ أَبِي أَيُّوبَ، عَنْ سَعِيدِ بْنِ جُبَيْرٍ: كُلُّ شَجَرَةٍ لَا سَاقَ لَهَا فَهِيَ مِنَ الْيَقْطِينِ.

وَفِي رِوَايَةٍ عَنْهُ: كُلُّ شَجَرَةٍ تَهْلِكُ مِنْ عَامِهَا فَهِيَ مِنَ الْيَقْطِينِ.

وَذَكَرَ بَعْضُهُمْ فِي الْقَرْعِ فَوَائِدَ، مِنْهَا: سُرْعَةُ نَبَاتِهِ، وَتَظْلِيلُ وَرَقِهِ لِكِبَرِهِ، وَنُعُومَتُهُ، وَأَنَّهُ لَا يَقْرَبُهُ الذُّبَابُ، وَجَوْدَةُ أَغْذِيَةِ ثَمَرِهِ، وَأَنَّهُ يُؤْكَلُ نِيئًا وَمَطْبُوخًا بِلُبِّهِ وَقِشْرِهِ أَيْضًا. وَقَدْ ثَبَتَ أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ ﷺ كَانَ يُحِبُّ الدُّبَّاءَ، وَيَتَتَبَّعُهُ مِنْ حَوَاشِي الصَّحْفَةِ. [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in his Sahih, no. 5439, from the hadith of Anas ibn Malik, may Allah be pleased with him.]]

* *

وَقَوْلُهُ تَعَالَى: ﴿وَأَرْسَلْنَاهُ إِلَى مِائَةِ أَلْفٍ أَوْ يَزِيدُونَ﴾ رَوَى شَهْرُ بْنُ حَوْشَبٍ، عَنِ ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ أَنَّهُ قَالَ: إِنَّمَا كَانَتْ رِسَالَةُ يُونُسَ بَعْدَ مَا نَبَذَهُ الْحُوتُ. رَوَاهُ ابْنُ جَرِيرٍ: حَدَّثَنِي الْحَارِثُ قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا الْحَسَنُ قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا أَبُو هِلَالٍ، عَنْ شَهْرٍ، بِهِ.

وَقَالَ ابْنُ أَبِي نَجِيحٍ، عَنْ مُجَاهِدٍ: أُرْسِلَ إِلَيْهِمْ قَبْلَ أَنْ يَلْتَقِمَهُ الْحُوتُ.

قُلْتُ: وَلَا مَانِعَ أَنْ يَكُونَ الَّذِينَ أُرْسِلَ إِلَيْهِمْ أَوَّلًا أُمِرَ بِالْعَوْدِ إِلَيْهِمْ بَعْدَ خُرُوجِهِ مِنَ الْحُوتِ، فَصَدَّقُوهُ كُلُّهُمْ وَآمَنُوا بِهِ. وَحَكَى الْبَغَوِيُّ أَنَّهُ أُرْسِلَ إِلَى أُمَّةٍ أُخْرَى بَعْدَ خُرُوجِهِ مِنَ الْحُوتِ، كَانُوا مِائَةَ أَلْفٍ أَوْ يَزِيدُونَ.

* *

وَقَوْلُهُ: ﴿أَوْ يَزِيدُونَ﴾ قَالَ ابْنُ عَبَّاسٍ -فِي رِوَايَةٍ عَنْهُ-: بَلْ يَزِيدُونَ، وَكَانُوا مِائَةً وَثَلَاثِينَ أَلْفًا.

وَعَنْهُ: مِائَةَ أَلْفٍ وَبِضْعَةً وَثَلَاثِينَ أَلْفًا. وَعَنْهُ: مِائَةَ أَلْفٍ وَبِضْعَةً وَأَرْبَعِينَ أَلْفًا.

وَقَالَ سَعِيدُ بْنُ جُبَيْرٍ: يَزِيدُونَ سَبْعِينَ أَلْفًا.

وَقَالَ مَكْحُولٌ: كَانُوا مِائَةَ أَلْفٍ وَعَشَرَةَ آلَافٍ. رَوَاهُ ابْنُ أَبِي حَاتِمٍ.

وَقَالَ ابْنُ جَرِيرٍ: حَدَّثَنَا مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ الرَّحِيمِ الْبَرْقِيُّ، حَدَّثَنَا عَمْرُو بْنُ أَبِي سَلَمَةَ قَالَ: سَمِعْتُ زُهَيْرًا عَمَّنْ سَمِعَ أَبَا الْعَالِيَةِ قَالَ: حَدَّثَنِي أُبَيُّ بْنُ كَعْبٍ: أَنَّهُ سَأَلَ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ ﷺ عَنْ قَوْلِهِ: ﴿وَأَرْسَلْنَاهُ إِلَى مِائَةِ أَلْفٍ أَوْ يَزِيدُونَ﴾، قَالَ: "يَزِيدُونَ عِشْرِينَ أَلْفًا". [[Tafsir al-Tabari (23/67).]]

وَرَوَاهُ التِّرْمِذِيُّ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ حُجْرٍ، عَنِ الْوَلِيدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ، عَنْ زُهَيْرٍ، عَنْ رَجُلٍ، عَنْ أَبِي الْعَالِيَةِ، عَنْ أُبَيِّ بْنِ كَعْبٍ، بِهِ، وَقَالَ: غَرِيبٌ. وَرَوَاهُ ابْنُ أَبِي حَاتِمٍ مِنْ حَدِيثِ زُهَيْرٍ، بِهِ. [[Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. 3229.]]

قَالَ ابْنُ جَرِيرٍ: وَكَانَ بَعْضُ أَهْلِ الْعَرَبِيَّةِ مِنْ أَهْلِ الْبَصْرَةِ يَقُولُ فِي ذَلِكَ: مَعْنَاهُ: إِلَى الْمِائَةِ الْأَلْفِ، أَوْ كَانُوا يَزِيدُونَ عِنْدَكُمْ، يَقُولُ: كَذَلِكَ كَانُوا عِنْدَكُمْ.

وَهَكَذَا سَلَكَ ابْنُ جَرِيرٍ هَاهُنَا مَا سَلَكَهُ عِنْدَ قَوْلِهِ تَعَالَى: ﴿ثُمَّ قَسَتْ قُلُوبُكُمْ مِنْ بَعْدِ ذَلِكَ فَهِيَ كَالْحِجَارَةِ أَوْ أَشَدُّ قَسْوَةً﴾ [البقرة: 74]، وَقَوْلِهِ: ﴿إِذَا فَرِيقٌ مِنْهُمْ يَخْشَوْنَ النَّاسَ كَخَشْيَةِ اللَّهِ أَوْ أَشَدَّ خَشْيَةً﴾ [النساء: 77]، وَقَوْلِهِ: ﴿فَكَانَ قَابَ قَوْسَيْنِ أَوْ أَدْنَى﴾ [النجم: 9]، أَنَّ الْمُرَادَ لَيْسَ أَنْقَصَ مِنْ ذَلِكَ، بَلْ أَزْيَدُ.

وَقَوْلُهُ: ﴿فَآمَنُوا﴾ أَيْ: فَآمَنَ هَؤُلَاءِ الْقَوْمُ الَّذِينَ أُرْسِلَ إِلَيْهِمْ يُونُسُ، عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ، جَمِيعُهُمْ. ﴿فَمَتَّعْنَاهُمْ إِلَى حِينٍ﴾ أَيْ: إِلَى وَقْتِ آجَالِهِمْ، كَقَوْلِهِ: ﴿فَلَوْلا كَانَتْ قَرْيَةٌ آمَنَتْ فَنَفَعَهَا إِيمَانُهَا إِلا قَوْمَ يُونُسَ لَمَّا آمَنُوا كَشَفْنَا عَنْهُمْ عَذَابَ الْخِزْيِ فِي الْحَيَاةِ الدُّنْيَا وَمَتَّعْنَاهُمْ إِلَى حِينٍ﴾ [يونس: 98].

God, the Exalted, says, rebuking these polytheists for attributing daughters to Allah, glorified is He, while they have for themselves what they desire, that is, males. That is, they wish for the best for themselves. ﴿When one of them is given the good news of a female, his face becomes dark, and he suppresses his grief﴾ [An-Nahl: 58]. That is, that news displeases him, and he chooses for himself only sons. God, the Exalted, says: How then do they attribute to Allah [the Exalted] the category that they themselves do not choose for themselves? Therefore He said: ﴿So ask them﴾, that is, ask them in a manner of rebuke: ﴿Has your Lord then daughters and they have sons?﴾, like His saying: ﴿Is it for you the male and for Him the female? That, then, is an unfair division﴾ [An-Najm: 21-22].

* *

His saying: ﴿Or did We create the angels as females while they were witnesses?﴾, that is, how did they pass judgment that the angels are females when they did not witness their creation? Like His saying: ﴿And they made the angels, who are servants of the Most Merciful, females. Did they witness their creation? Their testimony will be recorded and they will be questioned﴾ [Az-Zukhruf: 19], that is, they will be questioned about that on the Day of Resurrection.

* *

His saying: ﴿Unquestionably, it is from their own lie that they say: "Allah has begotten"﴾, that is, from their falsehood, ﴿and indeed, they are liars﴾. So Allah mentioned from them three statements concerning the angels, all at the extreme of disbelief and falsehood. First, they made them daughters of Allah, thus attributing a child to Allah. Second, they made that child female. Third, they worshipped them besides Allah. Each of these alone is sufficient for eternal abiding in the Fire of Jahannam.

Then He said, rebuking them: ﴿Has He chosen daughters over sons?﴾, that is, what is it that prevents Him from choosing daughters rather than sons? Like His saying: ﴿Has your Lord then favored you with sons and taken for Himself from the angels females? Indeed, you utter a great saying﴾ [Al-Isra': 40]. Therefore He said: ﴿What is wrong with you? How do you judge?﴾, that is, do you not have intellects by which you reflect on what you say?

﴿Will you not then remember? Or do you have a clear authority?﴾, that is, a proof for what you say.

﴿Then bring your book, if you should be truthful﴾, that is, bring a proof for that which rests upon a scripture sent down from the heaven from Allah, that He has taken what you say, for what you say cannot be supported by reason; rather, reason does not permit it at all.

* *

His saying: ﴿And they have made between Him and the jinn a kinship﴾. Mujahid said: The polytheists said: "The angels are the daughters of Allah." Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, asked: "Then who are their mothers?" They said: "The daughters of the chieftains of the jinn." Qatadah and Ibn Zayd said likewise. Therefore Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿But the jinn have known that they will be brought forth﴾, that is, those who attributed that to them, ﴿indeed, they will be brought forth﴾, that is, indeed those who said that will be brought forth into the punishment on the Day of Reckoning, because of their lying, their fabrication, and their uttering of falsehood without knowledge.

Al-Awfi said, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His saying: ﴿And they have made between Him and the jinn a kinship﴾: He said: The enemies of Allah claimed that He, blessed and exalted, and Iblis were two brothers. Ibn Jarir related it.

* *

His saying: ﴿Glorified is Allah above what they describe﴾, that is, exalted, sanctified and freed from having any child, and from what the wrongdoing, deviating ones describe Him with, [exalted] far above that.

* *

His saying: ﴿Except the chosen servants of Allah﴾ is an exception that is disconnected (munqati'), and it is from an affirmative statement, unless the pronoun in His saying ﴿what they describe﴾ refers to all people, and then He excepted from them the sincere ones, who are those who follow the truth sent down upon every prophet and messenger. Ibn Jarir made this exception apply to His saying: ﴿Indeed, they will be brought forth. Except the chosen servants of Allah﴾, and there is consideration in what he said.

They did not bring it out by this route, and it is sound according to the conditions of the two Shaykhs (al-Bukhari and Muslim).

* *

His saying: ﴿So turn away from them for a time. And watch them, for they will soon see﴾

This is a confirmation of what preceded regarding this command.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 37, verse 180–182:

He, exalted is He, declares His own noble Self free and holy and clear of what the wrongdoers, the deniers, the transgressors say—exalted and sanctified is He far above their words, a great exaltation. For this reason He said: ﴿Glory be to your Lord, the Lord of Might, above what they describe﴾, meaning: the Possessor of might which cannot be attained, ﴿above what they describe﴾, meaning: above the saying of these transgressors who fabricate.

﴿And peace be upon the messengers﴾, meaning: the peace of Allah be upon them in this world and the Hereafter, because of the soundness of what they said about their Lord, and its correctness and truth.

﴿And praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds﴾, meaning: to Him belongs praise in the first and the last, in every state. Since tasbih (glorification) includes tanzih (declaring Allah free) and tabri'ah (absolving Him) from deficiency by direct indication (dalalat al-mutabaqa), and necessarily entails affirming perfection, just as hamd (praise) indicates the affirmation of attributes of perfection by direct indication and necessarily entails tanzih from deficiency, He joined the two in this place and in many places of the Qur'an. For this reason He said: ﴿Glory be to your Lord, the Lord of Might, above what they describe. And peace be upon the messengers. And praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds﴾.

Sa'id ibn Abi 'Arubah related from Qatadah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When you greet me with peace, then greet the messengers with peace, for I am only a messenger among the messengers." Thus Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it from the hadith of Sa'id, from him in this manner [Tafsir al-Tabari (23/74)].

Ibn Abi Hatim, may Allah have mercy on him, also traced it with a chain, saying: 'Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn al-Junayd narrated to us, Abu Bakr al-A'yan and Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Rahim Sa'iqah narrated to us, both saying: Husayn ibn Muhammad narrated to us, Shaiban narrated to us, from Qatadah who said: Anas ibn Malik narrated to us, from Abu Talhah who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When you greet me with peace, then greet the messengers with peace." [Ibn Mardawayh and Ibn Sa'd also narrated it, as in al-Durr al-Manthur (7/140), through the chain Sa'id from Qatadah from Anas from Abu Talhah, marfu'an.]

The Hafiz Abu Ya'la said: Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr narrated to us, Nuh narrated to us, Abu Harun narrated to us, from Abu Sa'id, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that when he wished to give the greeting of peace, he would say: ﴿Glory be to your Lord, the Lord of Might, above what they describe. And peace be upon the messengers. And praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds﴾, then he would give the greeting. Its chain is weak. [In its chain is 'Umarah ibn Juwayn, Abu Harun al-'Abdi, who is abandoned in hadith. Abu Ya'la narrated it in his Musnad (2/363) saying: Ishaq narrated to us, Hammad narrated to us, from Abu Harun in similar wording.]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: 'Ammar ibn Khalid al-Wasiti narrated to us, Shababah narrated to us, from Yunus ibn Abi Ishaq, from al-Sha'bi who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever wishes to be given the fullest measure of reward on the Day of Resurrection, let him say at the end of his gathering, when he wants to rise: ﴿Glory be to your Lord, the Lord of Might, above what they describe. And peace be upon the messengers. And praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds﴾." [al-Suyuti mentioned it in al-Durr (7/141) without attributing it to anyone else, and it is mursal.] It is also narrated through another connected chain, halted (mawquf) upon 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him.

Abu Muhammad al-Baghawi said in his Tafsir: Abu Sa'id Ahmad ibn Shurayh informed us, Abu Ishaq al-Tha'labi informed us, Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, Ahmad ibn Ja'far ibn Hamdan narrated to us, Ibrahim ibn Sahlawayh narrated to us, 'Ali ibn Muhammad al-Tanafisi narrated to us, Waki' narrated to us, from Thabit ibn Abi Safiyyah, from al-Asbagh ibn Nubatah, from 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: Whoever wishes to be given the fullest measure of reward on the Day of Resurrection, let his last words in his gathering be: ﴿Glory be to your Lord, the Lord of Might, above what they describe. And peace be upon the messengers. And praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds﴾. [Ma'alim al-Tanzil of al-Baghawi (7/66); al-Wahidi narrated it in al-Wasit (3/536) from al-Asbagh ibn Nubatah with the same chain, and the imams criticized al-Asbagh ibn Nubatah.]

Al-Tabarani narrated through the chain of 'Abd Allah ibn Sakhr ibn Anas, from 'Abd Allah ibn Zayd ibn Arqam, from his father, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that he said: "Whoever says after every prayer: ﴿Glory be to your Lord, the Lord of Might, above what they describe. And peace be upon the messengers. And praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds﴾ three times, he has measured out the fullest measure of reward." [al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (5/211) through 'Abd al-Mun'im ibn Bashir from 'Abd Allah ibn Muhammad al-Ansi, from 'Abd Allah ibn Zayd ibn Arqam, from his father, marfu'an. Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (10/103): "In it is 'Abd al-Mun'im ibn Bashir, who is extremely weak."]

Hadiths have also come concerning the expiation of the gathering (kaffarat al-majlis): "Subhanaka Allahumma wa bihamdika, la ilaha illa anta, astaghfiruka wa atubu ilayka." I have devoted a separate section to them, and it will be written here, Allah willing. [Thus, and I did not find it in the manuscripts. The hadiths on the expiation of the gathering came from a group of Companions and Successors, namely: 1- Abu Hurayrah: al-Tirmidhi in his Sunan, no. (3433), narrated: Abu 'Ubaydah ibn Abi al-Safar, Ahmad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Hamdani, informed us, Hajjaj ibn Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Ibn Jurayj said: Musa ibn 'Uqbah informed me, from Suhayl ibn Abi Salih, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever sits in a gathering and much idle talk occurs in it, and says before he rises from that gathering: 'Subhanaka Allahumma wa bihamdika, ashhadu an la ilaha illa anta, astaghfiruka wa atubu ilayka', he will be forgiven for what occurred in that gathering."

Ibn Kathir said: "Imam Ahmad, al-Bukhari, Muslim, Abu Hatim, Abu Zur'ah, al-Daraqutni and others gave it a defect (ta'lil), and they attributed the error in it to Ibn Jurayj," although Abu Dawud narrated it in his Sunan, no. (4858), through 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi 'Amr from Sa'id al-Maqburi from Abu Hurayrah in similar wording. 2- Abu Barzah al-Aslami: Abu Dawud in the Sunan, no. (4859), said: Muhammad ibn Hatim al-Jurjara'i and 'Uthman ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us, that 'Abdah ibn Sulayman informed them from al-Hajjaj ibn Dinar, from Abu Hashim, from Abu al-'Aliyah, from Abu Barzah al-Aslami who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to say toward the end when he wished to rise from the gathering: "Subhanaka Allahumma wa bihamdika, ashhadu an la ilaha illa anta, astaghfiruka wa atubu ilayka." A man said: "O Messenger of Allah, you are saying words you did not say before." He said: "They are an expiation for what occurs in the gathering." Al-Nasa'i narrated it in al-Sunan al-Kubra, no. (10259), and al-Hakim in al-Mustadrak (1/537), through al-Hajjaj ibn Dinar. 3- Rafi' ibn Khadij: al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan al-Kubra, no. (10260), said: 'Ubayd Allah ibn Ibrahim ibn Sa'd informed us, saying: Yunus ibn Muhammad narrated to us, Mus'ab ibn Hayyan, brother of Muqatil ibn Hayyan, narrated to us, from Muqatil ibn Hayyan, from al-Rabi' ibn Anas, from Abu al-'Aliyah al-Riyahi, from Rafi' ibn Khadij who said: Toward the end, when his Companions gathered around him and he wished to rise, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would say: "Subhanaka Allahumma wa bihamdika, ashhadu an la ilaha illa anta, astaghfiruka wa atubu ilayka, I have done evil and wronged myself, so forgive me, for none forgives sins except You." We said: "O Messenger of Allah, are these words something you have newly introduced?" He said: "Yes, Jibril, peace be upon him, came to me and said: 'O Muhammad, these are the expiations of the gathering.'" Al-Hakim narrated it in al-Mustadrak (1/537) through Yunus ibn Muhammad. 4- 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr ibn al-'As: Abu Dawud in the Sunan, no. (4857), said: Ahmad ibn Salih narrated to us, Ibn Wahb narrated to us, saying: 'Amr informed me that Sa'id ibn Hilal narrated to him that Sa'id ibn Abi Sa'id al-Maqburi narrated to him from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr ibn al-'As that he said: "Words which no one says in his gathering when he rises, three times, except that they expiate for him what occurred, and no one says them in a gathering of goodness or a gathering of remembrance except that they are sealed for him by them, as a seal is pressed upon a page: Subhanaka Allahumma wa bihamdika, la ilaha illa anta, astaghfiruka wa atubu ilayka."

Thus Abu Dawud narrated it as a mawquf report, but al-Tabarani narrated it through another route as marfu'. Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (10/142): "In it is Muhammad ibn Jami' al-'Attar, whom Ibn Hibban declared reliable and many others declared weak, and the rest of its narrators are narrators of the Sahih." 5- 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud: al-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (10/203) said: Ahmad ibn Zuhayr al-Tustari narrated to us, 'Uthman ibn Hafs al-Tumni narrated to us, Yahya ibn Kathir narrated to us, from 'Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib, from Abu 'Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami, from 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "The expiation of the gathering is that the servant says: 'Subhanaka Allahumma wa bihamdika, ashhadu an la ilaha illa Allah, astaghfiruka wa atubu ilayka.'" 6- 'A'ishah: al-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Awsat, no. (4611), "Majma' al-Bahrayn," said: Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Raqqam narrated to us, Ahmad ibn al-Miqdam al-'Ijli narrated to us, al-Nadr ibn Abi al-Nadr narrated to us, from 'Amr ibn 'Abd al-Jabbar, from al-Hakam ibn 'Utaybah, from Masruq, from 'A'ishah who said: When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) raised his head to the ceiling of the house, he would say: "Subhanaka Allahumma wa bihamdika, astaghfiruka wa atubu ilayka." 'A'ishah said: I asked him about them, and he said: "I have been commanded with them."

Al-Tabarani said: No one narrated it from al-Hakam except 'Amr, and no one narrated from him except al-Nadr; Abu al-Ash'ath alone narrated it. In its chain is one who is not known.

Al-Nasa'i narrated it in 'Amal al-Yawm wa al-Layla through another route: from Sa'id ibn al-Hakam, from Khallad ibn Sulayman, from Khalid ibn Abi 'Imran, from 'Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, from 'A'ishah who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did not sit in a gathering nor recite the Qur'an without concluding it with these words. I said: "O Messenger of Allah, I see you do not sit or recite Qur'an or pray without ending with these words." He said: "Yes, whoever says good, it is a seal upon that good, and whoever says evil, it is an expiation for it: Subhanaka Allahumma wa bihamdika, la ilaha illa anta, astaghfiruka wa atubu ilayka." 7- Jubayr ibn Mut'im: al-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (2/138) said: al-'Abbas ibn Hamdan al-Hanafi narrated to us, 'Abd al-Jabbar ibn al-'Ala' narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to me, Ibn 'Ajlan narrated to me, from Muslim ibn Abi Maryam, from Nafi' ibn Jubayr, from his father who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever says: 'Subhan Allah wa bihamdih, subhanaka Allahumma wa bihamdika, ashhadu an la ilaha illa anta, astaghfiruka wa atubu ilayka,' and says it in a gathering of remembrance, it is like a seal stamped upon it, and whoever says it in a gathering of idle talk, it is an expiation for it." Then he narrated it through Khalid ibn Yazid al-'Umari, from Dawud ibn Qays, from Nafi' ibn Jubayr in similar wording. 8- al-Zubayr ibn al-'Awwam: al-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Awsat, no. (4606), "Majma' al-Bahrayn," said: Muhammad ibn 'Ali al-Tara'ifi al-Raqqi narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated to us, al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn A'yan narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Salamah al-Nusaybi wrote mentioning that 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn Suhayb narrated to him from Khabbab, the mawla of al-Zubayr ibn al-'Awwam, from al-Zubayr who said: We said: "O Messenger of Allah, when we rise from your presence we begin discussing the talk of the Jahiliyyah." He said: "When you sit in those gatherings in which you fear for your souls, then say when you rise: 'Subhanaka Allahumma wa bihamdika, nashhadu an la ilaha illa anta, nastaghfiruka wa natubu ilayka,' and it will expiate for you what you have committed." Al-Tabarani said: It is not narrated from al-Zubayr except by this chain; Muhammad ibn 'Ali alone narrated it. In its chain is one who is not known. 9- Anas ibn Malik: al-Bazzar in his Musnad, no. (3123), "Kashf al-Astar," said: 'Umar ibn Musa al-Shami narrated to us, 'Uthman ibn Matar narrated to us, from Thabit, from Anas who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The expiation of the gathering is that you say: 'Subhanaka Allahumma wa bihamdika, astaghfiruka wa atubu ilayka.'" Al-Bazzar said: We do not know it being narrated from Anas except by this route, and 'Uthman is weak in hadith; Muslim and others narrated from him. Al-Tabarani narrated it in al-Awsat, no. (4610), "Majma' al-Bahrayn," through 'Uthman ibn Matar. 10- Umm Salamah: al-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Awsat, no. (4609), "Majma' al-Bahrayn," said: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Salm narrated to us, Sahl ibn 'Uthman narrated to us, Hafs ibn Ghiyath narrated to us, from 'Asim, from al-Sha'bi, from Umm Salamah who said: Before he died, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to say often: "Subhanaka Allahumma wa bihamdika, astaghfiruka wa atubu ilayka." I said: "O Messenger of Allah, I see you say often: 'Subhanaka Allahumma wa bihamdika, astaghfiruka wa atubu ilayka.'" He said: "I have been commanded with a matter," and he recited: "When there comes the help of Allah and the victory." Al-Tabarani said: No one narrated it from 'Asim except Hafs, and Sahl alone narrated it. 11- al-Sa'ib ibn Yazid: Imam Ahmad in his Musnad (3/450) said: Yunus narrated to us, from Layth, from Yazid, meaning Ibn al-Had, from Isma'il ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Ja'far who said: It reached me that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "No person sits in a gathering and says when he wishes to rise: 'Subhanaka Allahumma wa bihamdika, la ilaha illa anta, astaghfiruka wa atubu ilayka,' except that he is forgiven for what occurred in that gathering." Yazid ibn Khusayfah said: I narrated this hadith, and so al-Sa'ib ibn Yazid narrated it to me from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Al-Tabarani narrated it in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (7/154) through Layth. Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (10/141): "Its narrators are narrators of the Sahih." 12- Isma'il ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Ja'far: The context of his hadith is the one before it, and it is mursal. 13- 'Umar ibn al-Khattab: I have not found its chain, and he mentioned it...]

End of the tafsir of Surat al-Saffat.

He, exalted is He, declares His own noble Self free and holy and clear of what the wrongdoers, the deniers, the transgressors say—exalted and sanctified is He far above their words, a great exaltation. For this reason He said: ﴿Glory be to your Lord, the Lord of Might, above what they describe﴾, meaning: the Possessor of might which cannot be attained, ﴿above what they describe﴾, meaning: above the saying of these transgressors who fabricate.

﴿And peace be upon the messengers﴾, meaning: the peace of Allah be upon them in this world and the Hereafter, because of the soundness of what they said about their Lord, and its correctness and truth.

﴿And praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds﴾, meaning: to Him belongs praise in the first and the last, in every state. Since tasbih (glorification) includes tanzih (declaring Allah free) and tabri'ah (absolving Him) from deficiency by direct indication (dalalat al-mutabaqa), and necessarily entails affirming perfection, just as hamd (praise) indicates the affirmation of attributes of perfection by direct indication and necessarily entails tanzih from deficiency, He joined the two in this place and in many places of the Qur'an. For this reason He said: ﴿Glory be to your Lord, the Lord of Might, above what they describe. And peace be upon the messengers. And praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds﴾.

Sa'id ibn Abi 'Arubah related from Qatadah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When you greet me with peace, then greet the messengers with peace, for I am only a messenger among the messengers." Thus Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it from the hadith of Sa'id, from him in this manner [Tafsir al-Tabari (23/74)].

Ibn Abi Hatim, may Allah have mercy on him, also traced it with a chain, saying: 'Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn al-Junayd narrated to us, Abu Bakr al-A'yan and Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Rahim Sa'iqah narrated to us, both saying: Husayn ibn Muhammad narrated to us, Shaiban narrated to us, from Qatadah who said: Anas ibn Malik narrated to us, from Abu Talhah who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When you greet me with peace, then greet the messengers with peace." [Ibn Mardawayh and Ibn Sa'd also narrated it, as in al-Durr al-Manthur (7/140), through the chain Sa'id from Qatadah from Anas from Abu Talhah, marfu'an.]

The Hafiz Abu Ya'la said: Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr narrated to us, Nuh narrated to us, Abu Harun narrated to us, from Abu Sa'id, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that when he wished to give the greeting of peace, he would say: ﴿Glory be to your Lord, the Lord of Might, above what they describe. And peace be upon the messengers. And praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds﴾, then he would give the greeting. Its chain is weak. [In its chain is 'Umarah ibn Juwayn, Abu Harun al-'Abdi, who is abandoned in hadith. Abu Ya'la narrated it in his Musnad (2/363) saying: Ishaq narrated to us, Hammad narrated to us, from Abu Harun in similar wording.]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: 'Ammar ibn Khalid al-Wasiti narrated to us, Shababah narrated to us, from Yunus ibn Abi Ishaq, from al-Sha'bi who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever wishes to be given the fullest measure of reward on the Day of Resurrection, let him say at the end of his gathering, when he wants to rise: ﴿Glory be to your Lord, the Lord of Might, above what they describe. [al-Suyuti mentioned it in al-Durr (7/141) without attributing it to anyone else, and it is mursal.] It is also narrated through another connected chain, halted (mawquf) upon 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him.

Abu Muhammad al-Baghawi said in his Tafsir: Abu Sa'id Ahmad ibn Shurayh informed us, Abu Ishaq al-Tha'labi informed us, Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, Ahmad ibn Ja'far ibn Hamdan narrated to us, Ibrahim ibn Sahlawayh narrated to us, 'Ali ibn Muhammad al-Tanafisi narrated to us, Waki' narrated to us, from Thabit ibn Abi Safiyyah, from al-Asbagh ibn Nubatah, from 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: Whoever wishes to be given the fullest measure of reward on the Day of Resurrection, let his last words in his gathering be: ﴿Glory be to your Lord, the Lord of Might, above what they describe. And peace be upon the messengers. And praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds﴾. [Ma'alim al-Tanzil of al-Baghawi (7/66); al-Wahidi narrated it in al-Wasit (3/536) from al-Asbagh ibn Nubatah with the same chain, and the imams criticized al-Asbagh ibn Nubatah.]

Al-Tabarani narrated through the chain of 'Abd Allah ibn Sakhr ibn Anas, from 'Abd Allah ibn Zayd ibn Arqam, from his father, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that he said: "Whoever says after every prayer: ﴿Glory be to your Lord, the Lord of Might, above what they describe. And peace be upon the messengers. And praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds﴾ three times, he has measured out the fullest measure of reward." [al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (5/211) through 'Abd al-Mun'im ibn Bashir from 'Abd Allah ibn Muhammad al-Ansi, from 'Abd Allah ibn Zayd ibn Arqam, from his father, marfu'an. Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (10/103): "In it is 'Abd al-Mun'im ibn Bashir, who is extremely weak."]

I have devoted a separate section to them, and it will be written here, Allah willing. [Thus, and I did not find it in the manuscripts. The hadiths on the expiation of the gathering came from a group of Companions and Successors, namely: 1- Abu Hurayrah: al-Tirmidhi in his Sunan, no. (3433), narrated: Abu 'Ubaydah ibn Abi al-Safar, Ahmad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Hamdani, informed us, Hajjaj ibn Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Ibn Jurayj said: Musa ibn 'Uqbah informed me, from Suhayl ibn Abi Salih, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever sits in a gathering and much idle talk occurs in it, and says before he rises from that gathering: 'Subhanaka Allahumma wa bihamdika, ashhadu an la ilaha illa anta, astaghfiruka wa atubu ilayka', he will be forgiven for what occurred in that gathering."

Ibn Kathir said: "Imam Ahmad, al-Bukhari, Muslim, Abu Hatim, Abu Zur'ah, al-Daraqutni and others gave it a defect (ta'lil), and they attributed the error in it to Ibn Jurayj," although Abu Dawud narrated it in his Sunan, no. (4858), through 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi 'Amr from Sa'id al-Maqburi from Abu Hurayrah in similar wording. 2- Abu Barzah al-Aslami: Abu Dawud in the Sunan, no. (4859), said: Muhammad ibn Hatim al-Jurjara'i and 'Uthman ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us, that 'Abdah ibn Sulayman informed them from al-Hajjaj ibn Dinar, from Abu Hashim, from Abu al-'Aliyah, from Abu Barzah al-Aslami who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to say toward the end when he wished to rise from the gathering: "Subhanaka Allahumma wa bihamdika, ashhadu an la ilaha illa anta, astaghfiruka wa atubu ilayka." A man said: "O Messenger of Allah, you are saying words you did not say before." He said: "They are an expiation for what occurs in the gathering." Al-Nasa'i narrated it in al-Sunan al-Kubra, no. (10259), and al-Hakim in al-Mustadrak (1/537), through al-Hajjaj ibn Dinar. 3- Rafi' ibn Khadij: al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan al-Kubra, no. (10260), said: 'Ubayd Allah ibn Ibrahim ibn Sa'd informed us, saying: Yunus ibn Muhammad narrated to us, Mus'ab ibn Hayyan, brother of Muqatil ibn Hayyan, narrated to us, from Muqatil ibn Hayyan, from al-Rabi' ibn Anas, from Abu al-'Aliyah al-Riyahi, from Rafi' ibn Khadij who said: Toward the end, when his Companions gathered around him and he wished to rise, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would say: "Subhanaka Allahumma wa bihamdika, ashhadu an la ilaha illa anta, astaghfiruka wa atubu ilayka, I have done evil and wronged myself, so forgive me, for none forgives sins except You." We said: "O Messenger of Allah, are these words something you have newly introduced?" He said: "Yes, Jibril, peace be upon him, came to me and said: 'O Muhammad, these are the expiations of the gathering.'" Al-Hakim narrated it in al-Mustadrak (1/537) through Yunus ibn Muhammad. 4- 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr ibn al-'As: Abu Dawud in the Sunan, no. (4857), said: Ahmad ibn Salih narrated to us, Ibn Wahb narrated to us, saying: 'Amr informed me that Sa'id ibn Hilal narrated to him that Sa'id ibn Abi Sa'id al-Maqburi narrated to him from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr ibn al-'As that he said: "Words which no one says in his gathering when he rises, three times, except that they expiate for him what occurred, and no one says them in a gathering of goodness or a gathering of remembrance except that they are sealed for him by them, as a seal is pressed upon a page: Subhanaka Allahumma wa bihamdika, la ilaha illa anta, astaghfiruka wa atubu ilayka."

Thus Abu Dawud narrated it as a mawquf report, but al-Tabarani narrated it through another route as marfu'. Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (10/142): "In it is Muhammad ibn Jami' al-'Attar, whom Ibn Hibban declared reliable and many others declared weak, and the rest of its narrators are narrators of the Sahih." 5- 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud: al-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (10/203) said: Ahmad ibn Zuhayr al-Tustari narrated to us, 'Uthman ibn Hafs al-Tumni narrated to us, Yahya ibn Kathir narrated to us, from 'Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib, from Abu 'Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami, from 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "The expiation of the gathering is that the servant says: 'Subhanaka Allahumma wa bihamdika, ashhadu an la ilaha illa Allah, astaghfiruka wa atubu ilayka.'" 6- 'A'ishah: al-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Awsat, no. (4611), "Majma' al-Bahrayn," said: Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Raqqam narrated to us, Ahmad ibn al-Miqdam al-'Ijli narrated to us, al-Nadr ibn Abi al-Nadr narrated to us, from 'Amr ibn 'Abd al-Jabbar, from al-Hakam ibn 'Utaybah, from Masruq, from 'A'ishah who said: When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) raised his head to the ceiling of the house, he would say: "Subhanaka Allahumma wa bihamdika, astaghfiruka wa atubu ilayka." Then he narrated it through Khalid ibn Yazid al-'Umari, from Dawud ibn Qays, from Nafi' ibn Jubayr in similar wording. 8- al-Zubayr ibn al-'Awwam: al-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Awsat, no. (4606), "Majma' al-Bahrayn," said: Muhammad ibn 'Ali al-Tara'ifi al-Raqqi narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated to us, al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn A'yan narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Salamah al-Nusaybi wrote mentioning that 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn Suhayb narrated to him from Khabbab, the mawla of al-Zubayr ibn al-'Awwam, from al-Zubayr who said: We said: "O Messenger of Allah, when we rise from your presence we begin discussing the talk of the Jahiliyyah." He said: "When you sit in those gatherings in which you fear for your souls, then say when you rise: 'Subhanaka Allahumma wa bihamdika, nashhadu an la ilaha illa anta, nastaghfiruka wa natubu ilayka,' and it will expiate for you what you have committed." (4610), "Majma' al-Bahrayn," through 'Uthman ibn Matar. 10- Umm Salamah: al-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Awsat, no. (4609), "Majma' al-Bahrayn," said: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Salm narrated to us, Sahl ibn 'Uthman narrated to us, Hafs ibn Ghiyath narrated to us, from 'Asim, from al-Sha'bi, from Umm Salamah who said: Before he died, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to say often: "Subhanaka Allahumma wa bihamdika, astaghfiruka wa atubu ilayka." I said: "O Messenger of Allah, I see you say often: 'Subhanaka Allahumma wa bihamdika, astaghfiruka wa atubu ilayka.'" Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 37, verse 180–182:

He, exalted is He, declares His own noble Self free and holy and clear of what the wrongdoers, the deniers, the transgressors say—exalted and sanctified is He far above their words, a great exaltation. For this reason He said: ﴿Glory be to your Lord, the Lord of Might, above what they describe﴾, meaning: the Possessor of might which cannot be attained, ﴿above what they describe﴾, meaning: above the saying of these transgressors who fabricate.

﴿And peace be upon the messengers﴾, meaning: the peace of Allah be upon them in this world and the Hereafter, because of the soundness of what they said about their Lord, and its correctness and truth.

﴿And praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds﴾, meaning: to Him belongs praise in the first and the last, in every state. Since tasbih (glorification) includes tanzih (declaring Allah free) and tabri'ah (absolving Him) from deficiency by direct indication (dalalat al-mutabaqa), and necessarily entails affirming perfection, just as hamd (praise) indicates the affirmation of attributes of perfection by direct indication and necessarily entails tanzih from deficiency, He joined the two in this place and in many places of the Qur'an. For this reason He said: ﴿Glory be to your Lord, the Lord of Might, above what they describe. And peace be upon the messengers. And praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds﴾.

Sa'id ibn Abi 'Arubah related from Qatadah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When you greet me with peace, then greet the messengers with peace, for I am only a messenger among the messengers." Thus Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it from the hadith of Sa'id, from him in this manner [Tafsir al-Tabari (23/74)].

Ibn Abi Hatim, may Allah have mercy on him, also traced it with a chain, saying: 'Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn al-Junayd narrated to us, Abu Bakr al-A'yan and Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Rahim Sa'iqah narrated to us, both saying: Husayn ibn Muhammad narrated to us, Shaiban narrated to us, from Qatadah who said: Anas ibn Malik narrated to us, from Abu Talhah who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When you greet me with peace, then greet the messengers with peace." [Ibn Mardawayh and Ibn Sa'd also narrated it, as in al-Durr al-Manthur (7/140), through the chain Sa'id from Qatadah from Anas from Abu Talhah, marfu'an.]

The Hafiz Abu Ya'la said: Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr narrated to us, Nuh narrated to us, Abu Harun narrated to us, from Abu Sa'id, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that when he wished to give the greeting of peace, he would say: ﴿Glory be to your Lord, the Lord of Might, above what they describe. And peace be upon the messengers. And praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds﴾, then he would give the greeting. Its chain is weak. [In its chain is 'Umarah ibn Juwayn, Abu Harun al-'Abdi, who is abandoned in hadith. Abu Ya'la narrated it in his Musnad (2/363) saying: Ishaq narrated to us, Hammad narrated to us, from Abu Harun in similar wording.]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: 'Ammar ibn Khalid al-Wasiti narrated to us, Shababah narrated to us, from Yunus ibn Abi Ishaq, from al-Sha'bi who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever wishes to be given the fullest measure of reward on the Day of Resurrection, let him say at the end of his gathering, when he wants to rise: ﴿Glory be to your Lord, the Lord of Might, above what they describe. And peace be upon the messengers. And praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds﴾." [al-Suyuti mentioned it in al-Durr (7/141) without attributing it to anyone else, and it is mursal.] It is also narrated through another connected chain, halted (mawquf) upon 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him.

Abu Muhammad al-Baghawi said in his Tafsir: Abu Sa'id Ahmad ibn Shurayh informed us, Abu Ishaq al-Tha'labi informed us, Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, Ahmad ibn Ja'far ibn Hamdan narrated to us, Ibrahim ibn Sahlawayh narrated to us, 'Ali ibn Muhammad al-Tanafisi narrated to us, Waki' narrated to us, from Thabit ibn Abi Safiyyah, from al-Asbagh ibn Nubatah, from 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: Whoever wishes to be given the fullest measure of reward on the Day of Resurrection, let his last words in his gathering be: ﴿Glory be to your Lord, the Lord of Might, above what they describe. And peace be upon the messengers. And praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds﴾. [Ma'alim al-Tanzil of al-Baghawi (7/66); al-Wahidi narrated it in al-Wasit (3/536) from al-Asbagh ibn Nubatah with the same chain, and the imams criticized al-Asbagh ibn Nubatah.]

Al-Tabarani narrated through the chain of 'Abd Allah ibn Sakhr ibn Anas, from 'Abd Allah ibn Zayd ibn Arqam, from his father, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that he said: "Whoever says after every prayer: ﴿Glory be to your Lord, the Lord of Might, above what they describe. And peace be upon the messengers. And praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds﴾ three times, he has measured out the fullest measure of reward." [al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (5/211) through 'Abd al-Mun'im ibn Bashir from 'Abd Allah ibn Muhammad al-Ansi, from 'Abd Allah ibn Zayd ibn Arqam, from his father, marfu'an. Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (10/103): "In it is 'Abd al-Mun'im ibn Bashir, who is extremely weak."]

Hadiths have also come concerning the expiation of the gathering (kaffarat al-majlis): "Subhanaka Allahumma wa bihamdika, la ilaha illa anta, astaghfiruka wa atubu ilayka." I have devoted a separate section to them, and it will be written here, Allah willing. [Thus, and I did not find it in the manuscripts. The hadiths on the expiation of the gathering came from a group of Companions and Successors, namely: 1- Abu Hurayrah: al-Tirmidhi in his Sunan, no. (3433), narrated: Abu 'Ubaydah ibn Abi al-Safar, Ahmad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Hamdani, informed us, Hajjaj ibn Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Ibn Jurayj said: Musa ibn 'Uqbah informed me, from Suhayl ibn Abi Salih, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever sits in a gathering and much idle talk occurs in it, and says before he rises from that gathering: 'Subhanaka Allahumma wa bihamdika, ashhadu an la ilaha illa anta, astaghfiruka wa atubu ilayka', he will be forgiven for what occurred in that gathering."

Ibn Kathir said: "Imam Ahmad, al-Bukhari, Muslim, Abu Hatim, Abu Zur'ah, al-Daraqutni and others gave it a defect (ta'lil), and they attributed the error in it to Ibn Jurayj," although Abu Dawud narrated it in his Sunan, no. (4858), through 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi 'Amr from Sa'id al-Maqburi from Abu Hurayrah in similar wording. 2- Abu Barzah al-Aslami: Abu Dawud in the Sunan, no. A man said: "O Messenger of Allah, you are saying words you did not say before." He said: "They are an expiation for what occurs in the gathering." Al-Nasa'i narrated it in al-Sunan al-Kubra, no.
